In such a case the only recourse is\h\h to remind creationists at every opportunity\h possible that they are believing in magic.\h Let’s now pivot to paleontology and the fossil\h record, because this is the primary line of\h\h evidence that substantiates everything we are\h describing. All of these lineages on the tree of\h\h life are immaculately supported by the millions\h of fossilized specimens that have been found,\h\h which can be accurately dated to specific time\h periods and which populate all of these branches,\h\h thus elucidating the forms which have existed in\h the past, as well as their gradual morphological\h\h change. Of course the fossil record is\h not perfect, because fossilization is a\h\h relatively rare occurrence. We will never have\h fossils for every single species that has ever\h\h existed. But if we are doing a very large jigsaw\h puzzle, we will be able to tell what the picture\h\h is without every single last puzzle piece. First of all, what is a fossil? A fossil is\h\h the preserved remains of an organism or some kind\h of evidence of its behavior that is found in rock,\h\h soil, or amber, that is over 10,000\h years old. These can be very large,\h\h if preserving a large animal, or they can be very\h small, preserving even microorganisms. The reason\h\h these are rare is that dead organisms tend to\h decay very quickly, so this kind of preservation\h\h occurs during relatively uncommon events. The\h organism must be rapidly covered by sediment,\h\h so it might become buried by the sea floor, or\h lava, or tar. Once trapped within sediment, the\h\h body does decay, but bodily particles get replaced\h by minerals, especially in hard parts like bones,\h\h teeth, or shells. Once the organism is gone, its\h precise form remains preserved for us to find,\h\h so we can gather highly detailed information\h about their morphologies, and more. This is the\h\h most common type of fossilization and it works\h well with bony animals, but other processes\h\h can also occur, like insects getting trapped in\h resin or amber. This is one way that we can find\h\h the remains of soft-bodied organisms that don’t\h fossilize well. There are also trace fossils,\h\h which unlike the body fossils we just described,\h preserve the behavior of organisms. This would\h\h include things like footprints or burrows.\h Paleontologists study all of these fossils\h\h to learn about what kinds of living organisms\h lived, and when. Finding remains of aquatic\h\h animals in the middle of a desert tells us there\h was once water there, and so forth. And there are\h\h numerous methods of dating fossils, including\h radiometric dating as most are aware, but also\h\h electron spin resonance, thermoluminescence,\h and others. There is nothing speculative about\h\h the dates that we assign to fossilized remains. Creationists have many issues with fossilization,\h\h of course. First, they pretend fossilization\h should be impossible because geological processes\h\h are so slow. This is ironic, considering the\h lightning fast rates of sediment deposition\h\h they pretend are possible for the generation\h of post-flood geological structures. But\h\h nevertheless, as slow as sediment deposition\h typically is, other processes can be very fast.\h\h Rivers can flood suddenly. Tidal waves can occur.\h Volcanoes erupt. There are many violent processes\h\h that can rapidly bury organisms. These are not a\h daily occurrence, but over hundreds of millions\h\h of years, there are plenty of opportunities for\h burial and later fossilization by these means.\h\h Additionally, there are even slow methods of\h fossilization. Animals decay because of bacteria,\h\h but there are swampy anoxic regions where bacteria\h that decay organisms can’t survive, so animals can\h\h be slowly preserved as they are buried by sediment\h at a more typical rate. The same can be said\h\h for deoxygenated ocean basins, where decaying\h bacteria and larger scavengers can’t survive.\h Then of course the biggest problem is that\h creationists are in complete denial as to\h\h the extent of the fossil record. Way back in\h Darwin’s time we didn’t have a lot to work\h\h with. That’s why he explicitly stated that\h the success of his theory would hinge on\h\h whether paleontological evidence of transitional\h forms would be discovered. Over 150 years later,\h\h we have plenty to work with. The number\h and variety of specimens we have found is\h\h staggering. To present an exhaustive list of\h transitional species would require an entire\h\h series of videos unto itself, so we will not do\h that, but simply googling “list of transitional\h\h species” is enough to keep one occupied for\h days. Rather, we can highlight a handful of\h\h important ones to illustrate precisely why these\h specimens so remarkably substantiate evolution.\h\h Look at Ambulocetus. This is an early amphibious\h cetacean from a little under 50 million years ago,\h\h so this is along the lineage that produced modern\h whales. The transitional nature of its morphology\h\h is immaculate. It was able to walk on land roughly\h like a sea lion, and it swam somewhat like an\h\h otter, using its limbs as well as undulation for\h propulsion. It did not have a tail like whales do,\h\h but it may have had webbed feet. This is where\h Ambulocetus sits on the family tree in comparison\h\h to modern whales. And of course there are many\h other transitional species along this lineage\h\h ending with whales that we could look at, such as\h Basilosaurus, from around 40 million years ago.\h\h This is quite different from Ambulocetus, being\h that it was an early marine mammal, and it was\h\h fully aquatic. But we still see the intermediate\h morphological features that would lead to whales.\h We should make one thing clear at this point. In\h a certain sense, every species is a transitional\h\h species. There are no evolutionary dead\h ends apart from mass extinctions. Life\h\h is always changing. Some organisms fit\h an environmental niche extremely well,\h\h so if that environment changes very little, then\h certain forms can persist with very little change,\h\h such as with sharks. Shark diversity has grown\h incredibly over hundreds of millions of years,\h\h but there are certain sharks today which are very\h similar to ancient sharks, although smaller. But\h\h for the most part, change is always occurring.\h We say transitional species when referring to\h\h extinct species present on lineages that produced\h extant species. This is the difference between\h\h what paleontologists refer to as stem groups and\h crown groups. A crown group includes the most\h\h recent common ancestor of all the currently living\h members of a group plus all its descendants. A\h\h stem group includes exclusively extinct species\h that existed prior to the crown group and which\h\h do not share all the features of the crown group.\h There are species that are alive today that will\h\h one day be extinct, and they may at that point\h be considered transitional species from the\h\h perspective of scientists in that time. It is not\h the case that there are certain, special, perfect\h\h forms that are somehow the goal of evolution, and\h inferior species that have to be traversed to get\h\h from one perfect form to another. It’s just\h what has existed in the past and what exists\h\h today. Ambulocetus is not inherently inferior to\h modern whales, there are many factors that go into\h\h extinctions, and one day whales will go extinct\h as well. But we can use the fossil record to\h\h understand how it is related to other mammals,\h and other animals in general. It is the case\h\h that the closest living relatives of whales are\h hippos. This does not mean hippos are ancestors\h\h of whales. It means that hippos and whales share\h a common ancestor that is more recent than the\h\h common ancestor of both hippos and whales with\h other mammals. Going backwards on the branches\h\h that led to hippos and whales would show us an\h ancestor with a totally different morphology,\h\h and distinct populations of this species produced\h different branches which diverged dramatically\h\h over tens of millions of years. This is one of the\h main concepts that creationists do not understand,\h\h and need to be taught with clarity. Those who resist this information use a\h\h number of tactics. First, they will simply deny\h the existence of transitional species. They can\h\h do this in a dishonest way by discussing the time\h of Darwin. For those who dare to\h examine this from a modern perspective,\h\h no matter what types of specimens are collected,\h or how many, they will refuse to accept them as\h\h being truly transitional. They will pretend that\h any fossilized organism must have been a version\h\h of what exists today. They will often bring up the Nebraska man.\h\h This was the name given to a putative hominid\h species based on a tooth that was found in 1917.\h\h By 1922 it was realized by the scientific\h community that it actually belonged to an\h\h extinct peccary species, which had been severely\h weathered such that it resembled a hominid tooth.\h\h This was a misidentification made by a singular\h paleontologist who specifically warned that it\h\h was not definitive proof of a hominid, but\h creationists pretend this singular mistake\h\h somehow invalidates all the hundreds of\h hominid specimens that are clear as day.\h They will also bring up the Piltdown man. This was\h a paleoanthropological fraud where bone fragments\h\h were presented by an amateur archeologist as\h belonging to an early hominid species. They were\h\h accepted for a while in Britain, but debunked just\h a few years later by the wider anthropological\h\h community. Creationists again use this singular\h incident to try to deny the entire field of\h\h biological anthropology, neglecting to acknowledge\h that it is simply an instance of fraud that was\h\h exposed by the scientific community itself.\h In the end, this is all creationists can do,\h\h make a fuss over nothing to deflect from an\h entire field of science they don’t want to exist,\h\h because we have firmly substantiated dozens of\h hominid species between modern humans and our\h\h most recent common ancestor with other apes,\h and there is not a single honest and educated\h\h person in the anthropological community who\h would pretend that all of them are somehow\h\h just chimps or people, due to the undeniable\h intermediary characteristics they possess.\h Another thing creationists do is they fixate\h on remaining gaps in the fossil record. This\h\h is for two reasons. First, they know, just as\h paleontologists do, that the fossil record will\h\h never be 100% complete. It is not likely\h that every single species was fossilized,\h\h and it is even less likely that we would find\h them all. They’re hard to find. That does not\h\h prevent us from filling in the fossil record\h thoroughly enough to make evolution and common\h\h descent consistent beyond reasonable doubt, just\h on the grounds of the fossil record alone. The\h\h other reason they do this is to use numbers in\h a tricky way. Let’s say there are two organisms,\h\h A and B, and the transition between them is a\h mystery. There is a gap in the fossil record.\h\h Then we find organism C, which immaculately fits\h the description of a transitional species between\h\h A and B. But what’s this! Now there are two gaps.\h How did we get from A to C, and from C to B? Then\h\h we find organisms D and E to fill those two gaps.\h Now there are four gaps! Things just keep getting\h\h worse and worse. Of course this is preposterous,\h filling in gaps like this corroborates an\h\h evolutionary lineage, and in the limit of hundreds\h of transitional species, the morphological gaps\h\h become smaller and smaller, such that to doubt\h their representation of an evolutionary lineage\h\h becomes more and more unreasonable. But\h creationists are not reasonable, so this is\h\h the game they play. An example is the transition\h from dinosaurs to modern birds. Archeopteryx was\h\h discovered way back in 1861, and presented as a\h feathered dinosaur along a lineage from raptors to\h\h birds. This was not enough for creationists, which\h is fair enough, but since then, countless other\h\h forms have been found more clearly outlining this\h lineage from two-legged dinosaurs to modern birds.\h\h The gradual change in morphology that can be seen\h is quite striking, and in fact, if one stares at\h\h an ostrich for long enough, the resemblance\h to dinosaurs like raptors is actually quite\h\h obvious. The real difference is the feathers,\h which evolved very easily from dermal placodes\h\h in a manner similar to scales, as they are\h both made of keratin. In fact, there is a point\h\h mutation that can occur in certain chickens that\h causes them to grow feathers instead of scales\h\h on their legs and feet, which makes them look\h pretty funny. Additionally, ectopic expression\h\h of the regulatory genes Spry2 and β-catenin\h in embryonic alligator skin produces bud-like\h\h structures that resemble avian long feather\h buds. These are just examples of how trivial\h\h it is to explain these types of changes, like\h scaly dinosaurs producing feathered birds. But\h\h we will discuss genetics in the next installment. Looking further at the fossil record as a whole,\h\h it presents enormous problems for creationists\h of all varieties. First, for those who believe\h\h that these specimens were deposited rapidly\h during sedimentation after a global flood,\h\h things get absurd very quickly. Of course these\h are dead organisms that were not on the ark,\h\h so they were all alive at the same time, died\h at the same time, and were deposited at the\h\h same time. The idea that all of these organisms\h were deposited into specific layers so flawlessly\h\h becomes a statistical impossibility.\h With regard to the Phanerozoic Eon,\h\h trilobites are present exclusively in the deepest\h layers and no others. Dinosaurs are in the middle\h\h layers and no others. Hominid remains are in the\h top layers and no others. Every type of organism\h\h is present in a narrow range of strata, which\h just happens to delineate gradual morphological\h\h change from basal forms to modern forms. Creationists make transparently desperate attempts\h\h to explain the distribution. One such idea is\h hydraulic sorting. They pretend the fossils\h\h are organized according to physical features\h like mass and buoyancy. This is ridiculous,\h\h as there is simply no correlation. Ammonites are\h very light and buoyant but they are present only\h\h in the bottom layers, because they are so\h ancient. Turtles are dense but are in the\h\h middle to higher layers. We can also look\h to discrepancies within forms. Trilobites\h\h come in a wide variety of sizes. Shouldn’t they\h therefore be spread out amongst the layers? But\h\h they’re all at the bottom. There is no physical\h characteristic that can possibly determine how\h\h these fossils were deposited simultaneously\h into very specific layers all around the world.\h Another strategy is to pretend that the separation\h depends on behavior. As the flood began to occur,\h\h marine animals remained towards the bottom since\h they were already underwater, slow moving reptiles\h\h who couldn’t run to higher ground got caught in\h the middle, and of course fast humans are at the\h\h top because they ran up some hills. This might\h trick children, but it becomes ridiculous once\h\h you broaden the scope. Why are marine mammals\h way up towards the top? Weren’t they swimming\h\h with the ancient sharks? Why are flowering plants\h up towards the top as well? Can trees run? There\h\h is clearly no broad correlation of this kind. So apart from the complete impossibility of\h\h sediment deposition happening so quickly in the\h first place, the idea that fossils would happen to\h\h coincidentally sort into the precise layers that\h coincide with evolutionary predictions, with no\h\h exceptions, is beyond ridiculous. It is abundantly\h clear that fossils exist in layers that correspond\h\h to time periods in which they were alive. There is\h no other explanation. So the creationist reaction\h\h is often then to simply lie about what we have\h determined scientifically. They look for anomalous\h\h geological features and pretend that they disprove\h all of paleontology. This would include thrust\h\h faults where rock layers are pushed up due to\h tectonic activity, so as to appear to be younger\h\h than they really are. Creationists present this as\h specimens in younger layers than we would predict.\h\h But any geologist can easily match these strata\h with other occurrences of the same strata as\h\h they normally occur, and the fossils line up just\h fine. Also in some cases these uplifting events\h\h fold sections of strata upside down, seemingly\h reversing the order of the strata, but we also\h\h find things like animal burrows upside down in\h these strata, as though they dug up instead of\h\h down. These are clear indicators that the strata\h have been inverted by some geological process. And\h\h the fact remains that anomalous data, even when\h unexplained, which these features are not, still\h\h would not be enough to negate the overwhelming\h patterns we see in the fossil record. At a certain\h\h point creationists have to simply pretend that\h paleontologists and geologists are lying. This is\h\h as weak a defense as can be imagined, but it does\h work on some people, so it’s the way they have\h\h to go. Scientists are evil, so just ignore all\h scientific data. The notion that\h\h such a gaslighting Ashton Kutcher-esque deity\h is all-loving or worthy of worship is rather\h\h comical. At the very least they just pretend that\h geological methods of dating are wrong, referring\h\h to an imagined tautology. The relative dating of\h strata is used to date fossils, and the fossils\h\h are used to date the layers, so it’s circular and\h unreliable. This is not the case, relative and\h\h absolute dating methods are completely different\h and they routinely corroborate each other. In the\h\h end, Young Earth creationists would have you\h believe that in 6000 years, over 99% of all\h\h life died, was rapidly deposited in sediments,\h and magically sorted itself into strata that\h\h couldn’t possibly have formed that fast and in a\h way that immaculately lines up with evolutionary\h\h principles even though evolution didn’t happen.\h It’s quite a leap of faith to say the least. In\h\h reality even a small child can understand that\h if we dig into lower strata, we go back in time,\h\h and we see things that are increasingly dissimilar\h to what we see today, along smooth morphological\h\h gradients that trace clear lineages over countless\h transitional forms for both plants and animals,\h\h that emerged and went extinct at certain\h times which match large-scale ecological\h\h events that are also well-substantiated. As bad as this all is for creationists,\h\h it gets even worse when you consider biogeography.\h This is the field that examines the geographical\h\h distribution of fossilized remains. As we already\h mentioned, certain forms are found exclusively in\h\h certain regions. This is obviously because they\h evolved in those regions. But creationists want\h\h us to believe that they walked from there all\h the way to the ark and then back, leaving no\h\h trace anywhere else. But we also now know due to\h plate tectonics that the continents were once all\h\h together. Combining predictions in geology with\h predictions in paleontology, if we know where\h\h the continents were once connected, and species\h that were around at that time, we should find\h\h the remains of those species in regions that are\h now nowhere near each other. This is a powerful\h\h prediction that was later confirmed, as we found\h remains of the same species in places like Western\h\h Africa and Eastern South America, as these once\h touched. This is what good science does, it brings\h\h together many different observations and explains\h them with a single model. That’s what evolution\h\h does to explain the sequence of fossilized remains\h as well as their locations, both stratigraphically\h\h and geographically. Everything fits precisely\h as expected, and in complete defiance of any\h\h expectation that creationists could have. For more elevated criticisms from intelligent\h\h design proponents, rather than lying about the\h existence of fossils or the geologic time they\h\h clearly outline, they will instead complain\h about portions of the fossil record that show\h\h morphological change which they claim is more\h rapid than evolutionary processes can explain,\h\h thus implying divine intervention. Of course\h the premiere example of this is the Cambrian\h\h explosion, which was a radiation event in which\h many new body plans first emerged. The dishonesty\h\h is more subtle here than with Young Earth\h creationists, but it is dishonesty nonetheless.\h\h First, they are always lying about the time\h spans. If pressed, they\h will say that it lasted 5-10 million years. Not so\h\h instantaneous anymore. But that is still a rather\h large lie. The truth is that this name can hardly\h\h be pinned down to a singular radiation event,\h so the term actually applies to more like 30-40\h\h million years, or even up to 80 million years\h according to some paleontologists. Furthermore,\h\h while it is true that many new body plans emerged,\h there are animal forms that seamlessly traversed\h\h the boundary between the Precambrian and Cambrian,\h so it is a far cry from the implication that\h\h all animal life suddenly exploded into\h existence. Speaking more generally\h\h about the rapidity of speciation, they will\h fixate on terms like punctuated equilibrium,\h\h which describes periods of more rapid change.\h First, creationists will pretend that this\h\h describes all of evolution, when evolution often\h occurs very gradually. We will\h\h see how this is not the case when we discuss\h molecular biology, such that there is plenty\h\h of time for evolutionary principles to operate. With the fossil record covered, let’s cover some\h\h more problems creationists face when trying to\h view the variety of life from a biblical lens.\h\h First, the people who wrote the bible were\h completely clueless when it comes to biology.\h\h Those who believe the bible was written by god\h are worshiping an allegedly omniscient god that\h\h had a practically non-existent understanding of\h his own creation. Leviticus 11:19 and Deuteronomy\h\h 14:18 say that bats are birds. They’re not,\h they’re mammals. Leviticus 11:20-23 says that\h\h some insects have four legs. They do not, they\h all have six. These are the writings of pre-scientific\h\h men with a tenuous grasp of the world around them. This becomes even more clear with the terminology\h\h that creationists tend to use. Creationists do\h not refer to phylogenetic taxa like kingdom,\h\h phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species.\h They just say “kinds”. They do this because the\h\h bible says kinds. At first glance this seems\h intuitive to someone who knows nothing about\h\h the animal kingdom. Dogs are a kind. Cats are\h a kind. Different kinds. Creationists differ in how\h they answer such questions, and they desperately\h\h hold on to the imprecision of the word kind\h for obvious reasons. On the ark, there were two\h\h animals of each kind. Kind never meant anything, and\h\h it still doesn’t mean anything, but it is used to\h deliberately obfuscate scientific principles. We have observed\h\h speciation events. We have physically observed a\h subpopulation of organisms diverge and generate\h\h a new species that is not interfertile with the\h original population. We have seen this for plants,\h\h like Spartina anglica, and Tragopogon mirus, as\h well as animals, like the fruit fly Drosophila\h\h paulistorum and the marbled crayfish Procambarus\h virginalis. Additionally there are ring species,\h\h like the Californian Ensatina salamanders,\h where a series of populations of organisms are\h\h connected by a geographic ring that represents\h a slow spreading out of a species, where two\h\h paths diverge and meet, or one path makes a full\h loop. The populations on both sides of the ring\h\h are interfertile with their immediate neighboring\h populations, but where the two arms meet up again,\h\h those populations are unable to interbreed. Enough\h time has passed and enough change has occurred\h\h during these slow radiations that what was once\h a single species has become different species.\h Of course in response to this, a creationist\h would say that kind does not mean species,\h\h those are just different types of salamanders,\h so they are all in the salamander kind. Therefore\h\h kind should be thought of as meaning genus, or\h even family. But then there is no problem in terms\h\h of what is brought forth, as any new species will\h continue to belong to the same greater taxa, so it\h\h is an example of organisms bringing forth of their\h kind, and also an example of new species arising\h\h due to evolution. This “kind” could be the primate\h kind, or the mammal kind, or the vertebrate kind,\h\h or the eukaryote kind. No matter what branching\h event we identify on the tree of life, there is\h\h a taxon that encompasses everything that results\h from that point forward, and thus qualifies as\h\h a singular kind. Humans and chimpanzees are\h both of the ape kind. Humans and elephants\h\h are both of the mammal kind. Humans and sharks\h are both of the vertebrate kind. Humans and trees\h\h are both of the eukaryote kind. Everything is the\h same kind if you take kind to mean any taxonomic\h\h label imaginable, so everything does indeed bring\h forth of its kind, and also evolution is true.\h This is one of the key things that creationists\h need to understand. Evolution operates in\h\h terms of nested hierarchies. Wherever branching\h occurs, we identify specific clades, and all the\h\h descendants of a particular common ancestor are\h part of the clade, and will continue to be part\h\h of that clade forever in the future. That’s why\h humans are technically primates, and tetrapods,\h\h and even fish. All land animals evolved from bony\h fish, diverging around 400 million years ago. We\h\h do not refer to ourselves as fish, rather we use\h the name Osteichthyes. This is the clade that\h\h includes all bony fish and all tetrapods. We’re\h in there. It is simply that we tend to define\h\h ourselves by more recent taxa, namely the genus\h and species, Homo sapiens. If populations continue\h\h to diverge and significant speciation events\h occur, we need new taxa, so we simply create new\h\h labels. It’s like nested folders in your computer.\h Within one large folder, like the animal kingdom,\h\h you can have many smaller folders, like all the\h different phyla. Each of those can have folders\h\h as well, which might be subphyla, or classes.\h Things can get very complicated and messy,\h\h but the hierarchy is always there, and if the\h documents in a folder become too numerous and\h\h diverse, you will likely create some new folders\h to further organize your documents. The same goes\h\h for phylogeny, which in the end is an arbitrary\h system of classification invented by humans.\h Things get trickier when considering\h interbreeding. Sometimes different species\h\h can interbreed. A horse and a donkey can make\h a mule. Typically such offspring are infertile.\h\h But sometimes they are fertile. Wolf/dog hybrids,\h bison/cattle hybrids, various birds, it absolutely\h\h can happen. Creationists would say that this\h challenges the biological definition of species,\h\h and with some justification. The definition can’t\h be applied flawlessly without exception, it’s just\h\h a guideline. Nature does not care about the words\h we use, it does what it does. But our inability to\h\h trap nature in our attempt at rigid categorization\h is in no way evidence against evolutionary\h\h principles. Populations diverge, sometimes\h retaining the ability to interbreed, sometimes\h\h losing that ability. It depends on the degree\h of divergence and the amount of time elapsed.\h Of course no matter what you tell a creationist,\h they will likely stick to their guns and say we’ve\h\h never seen life go all the way from a fish to a\h monkey. And of course they’re right. That took\h\h several hundred million years, and apart from the\h absurd timeframe, the odds of seeing that exact\h\h evolutionary lineage happen precisely as it did an\h additional time is like rolling ten million dice,\h\h marking the result, then rolling them again and\h expecting to get exactly the same result. It’s a\h\h statistical absurdity. But in general, that much\h change takes a really long time. That’s why we\h\h look to the fossil record to see what has already\h happened. Dogs and cats are different kinds,\h\h right? Well take a look at an extinct group of\h Carnivorans called miacids. They have primitive\h\h characteristics of both dogs and cats,\h like carnassial teeth. This is because\h\h these animals gave rise to both dogs and cats.\h Very close to the split between the two clades,\h\h differentiating members of one side from members\h of the other becomes very difficult. Take,\h\h for example, Cryptoprocta. This is on the feliform\h side so it’s more cat-like than dog-like, but the\h\h distinction is not trivial. Similarly, take a look\h at Moeritherium, one of the earliest ancestors of\h\h elephants, and Pezosiren, one of the earliest\h ancestors of manatees. They look very similar,\h\h having similar stocky bodies with short columnar\h legs, both having lived in freshwater bodies and\h\h consuming underwater plants. In general, such\h distinctions become more vague as we go into the\h\h past, closer to the common ancestor of two clades. This evidence is absolutely insurmountable. That’s\h\h why some creationists resort to simply denying\h anything they are told about past organisms and\h\h the fossil record. Once again, it’s all lies from\h the devil. They want to see something happening\h\h today, with their own eyes. Well very few can deny\h what humans have done with artificial selection.\h\h Unlike natural selection, which typically\h takes a very long time to produce significant\h\h morphological change, artificial selection\h can be quite rapid because it is guided by\h\h sentience. We can breed dogs in a deliberate way\h to rapidly enhance any arbitrary characteristic.\h\h All dogs were once like wolves. But we identified\h small differences and molded dogs into the breeds\h\h we see today, with an enormous range in size\h and behavior. We’ve done the same with plants\h\h in the form of crops. Virtually nothing in the\h produce section of the grocery store is natural,\h\h it’s all of human invention. We take things\h like Brassica oleracea, the wild mustard plant,\h\h and breed generations selectively with the intent\h of amplifying certain features of the plant. The\h\h result is broccoli, kale, cauliflower, cabbage,\h and Brussels sprouts. These look very different,\h\h but they all came from the same thing.\h Creationists will say a dog is still a dog\h\h and Brassica is still Brassica, but that’s not\h the point. Look at the degree of morphological\h\h change we can induce in just a few hundred years.\h The dog breeds are largely interfertile because we\h\h continue to forcibly breed them. But there would\h be a limit to this, which may arrive some time in\h\h the future, where we end up having to distinguish\h radically different breeds as different species.\h\h They certainly can seem that way, or they would\h if you had never seen a dog before. But of course\h\h creationists will not be satisfied, they want to\h see entirely new body plans. They want to see a\h\h dog sprout wings, or fins, or additional limbs.\h First of all, this is not a reasonable request.\h\h All primates, for example, have the same body\h plan. Technically, all mammals have the same\h\h body plan, just with significant modification.\h Speciation doesn’t require a whole new body\h\h plan. Humans and gorillas are obviously different\h species, but what is fundamentally different about\h\h us? How much more significant are the differences\h between humans and gorillas than the differences\h\h between dramatically different dog breeds?\h Certainly more, but not that much more. Beyond\h\h this, organisms can indeed develop additional\h limbs or new types of limbs very quickly, but\h\h this will require molecular biology to explain,\h so we will get there in the next installment.\h To continue briefly on this thread, we should\h elucidate some related creationist terminology.\h\h Creationists will sometimes try to seem scholarly\h by acknowledging that some evolution does occur,\h\h but in limited fashion. It is only\h variation within a kind. They will call\h\h this microevolution. Large scale evolution, or\h macroevolution, which creates totally new kinds,\h\h remains impossible. First, these are not\h scientific terms, at least not in the way\h\h that creationists use them. The only mention\h of them in the scientific literature is from\h\h Russian entomologist Yuri Filipchencko, who used\h the terms in a 1927 paper to distinguish between\h\h genetic change below the species level vs. above\h the species level, but this was written in a time\h\h when it was thought that all speciation requires\h macromutations, which we now know is not true. So\h\h creationists are the only people who use these\h terms, for the most part. But more importantly,\h\h as we just alluded to, the processes that result\h in all of these types of organismal changes are\h\h the same processes. Pretending that you can\h have a little evolution but not a lot is like\h\h pretending a leaky faucet could fill up a bucket\h but not a swimming pool. In reality, the faucet\h\h could fill up the Pacific Ocean, it just would\h take an incredibly long time. This is nothing\h\h but an ignorance of evolutionary mechanisms. Pivoting to another important demostration of\h\h evolution that creationists deny, we can discuss\h vestigial structures. Just as beneficial traits\h\h are selected for, traits that are no longer as\h useful tend to generate evolutionary pressures\h\h for their diminishment. But of course it is almost\h impossible for them to disappear without a trace,\h\h so we end up with tiny vestigial structures that\h are not a significant drain on energy resources,\h\h but represent what once was there. For example,\h whales have pelvic bones where lower limbs used to\h\h attach on their land-dwelling ancestors. It would\h be bizarre to think that a designer would give\h\h whales hip bones but no legs, yet it makes perfect\h sense in the context of evolution. Creationists\h\h will desperately cling to minor ancillary\h functions of vestigial structures and pretend\h\h those validate their existence in the context of\h design. Whale hip bones have some minor influence\h\h in reproductive behavior, but this does not negate\h the vestigial status. They do not do what they\h\h once did. It does some other minor thing, since\h nature is resourceful and makes the most of what\h\h it is working with. We can say the same thing for\h the remnants of leg bones in snakes, the human\h\h appendix, and more. To summarize, designating\h something as vestigial does not mean it is\h\h functionless, even though every creationist will\h bring up minor functions for vestigial structures\h\h in an attempt to disprove its vestigial status.\h Now you can correct them. Beyond this, there\h\h are plenty of functionless biological structures.\h Humans have auricular muscles for moving our ears,\h\h like all other mammals. Just the way that most\h cats and dogs can move their ears to point towards\h\h sounds, we have those muscles too. And while a\h few people can wiggle their ears as a party trick,\h\h we can’t actually aim our ears anywhere, despite\h the muscles for this function still existing,\h\h and even attempting to function when stimulated\h by sound, they are simply too weak to do\h\h anything. Their function has been completely lost. With that we have covered some important ground\h\h regarding evolutionary biology and paleontology.\h Helping creationists understand phylogeny and\h\h the tree of life is one of the most important\h things one can do to help them see what evolution\h\h actually proposes, rather than the cartoonish\h mischaracterizations that preachers promote,\h\h like porcupines magically morphing into fiddler\h crabs. But we have a lot more to cover still,\h\h because the real ammunition in obliterating\h creationist propaganda arrives when we dive\h\h into genetics and molecular biology,\h so let’s head in that direction next. So far in this series we have gone through the\h most common creationist talking points pertaining\h\h to cosmology, planetary science, abiogenesis,\h evolutionary biology, and paleontology. Let’s\h\h continue by zooming in to the molecular level,\h so that we can discuss evolution from the\h\h standpoint of genetics and molecular biology. Most creationists do not comprehend genetics\h\h on even a high school level. For this reason, it\h is very easy to run circles around less educated\h\h creationists within this unintuitive sphere. If\h they don’t understand what DNA is or what it does,\h\h it’s like shooting fish in a barrel. More\h sophisticated intelligent design proponents\h\h focus most of their propaganda on this area\h as well, because it is so much more esoteric,\h\h and lying with confidence about things\h that their targets don’t understand gives\h\h them a high probability of success. There’s\h lots to discuss here, so let’s get started.\h First we need to go over some background\h information. Creationists don’t understand\h\h genetics, but you should, so let’s hit the basics\h in ultra-abbreviated fashion. As always, I have\h\h tutorials on biochemistry and biology that explain\h everything we will discuss in greater detail,\h\h so head there after this series if you want to\h take the next step. For our purposes, let’s make\h\h sure we know what DNA is. DNA is a nucleic acid,\h which means it is a polymer of nucleotides. There\h\h are four different nucleotides in DNA, each made\h of a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base.\h\h These bases are abbreviated as A, T, C, and\h G. Nucleotides come together in different\h\h combinations to make DNA, which is made of two\h strands that coil together in a double helix,\h\h with the bases pointing towards each other in\h the interior. The way the two strands anneal is\h\h according to base pairing. A pairs with T and C\h with G. Every organism has a genome which is made\h\h of some number of chromosomes, which are very\h long DNA molecules with billions of base pairs,\h\h wrapped around proteins called histones.\h These chromosomes are the genetic code,\h\h which contains instructions for the assembly\h of the organism during embryonic development\h\h and its maintenance throughout its life. This occurs through transcription and translation.\h\h In transcription, small portions of the chromosome\h called genes are opened up by enzymes in order to\h\h generate an mRNA transcript. This occurs by\h the same rules of base pairing as for DNA,\h\h but mRNA is a little different. Then the mRNA is\h translated by a ribosome, again through simple\h\h base pairing, in order to generate a protein.\h This happens because the tRNA molecules that\h\h match up with the mRNA transcript, three bases\h at a time, are attached to specific amino acids,\h\h and the amino acids join together to form\h a polypeptide, which folds into a protein.\h\h Proteins do almost everything in your\h body. There are structural proteins,\h\h there are enzymes that do chemistry, there are\h receptor proteins that receive messages and\h\h trigger physiological functions, and so forth. One of the most important aspects of genetics\h\h for our purposes here is the way that the genome\h guides embryonic development to yield a particular\h\h type of animal. Unfortunately this is exceedingly\h complex, but we can at least describe Hox genes,\h\h which are a group of related genes that specify\h regions of the body plan along the head-tail axis\h\h of an animal. Encoded in these genes is the number\h and positions of limbs and other structures that\h\h will develop along the body. This is because\h the genes code for transcription factors,\h\h which are proteins that help turn other genes\h on and off by selectively binding to them, thus\h\h either promoting or inhibiting gene expression at\h hundreds of other sites on the genome. Because Hox\h\h genes have products that regulate so many other\h genes, changes to these genes can have dramatic\h\h effects on the developing organism’s body plan. With that covered, we now have to discuss\h\h mutations. Mutations describe changes to the\h genome. There are many different kinds of\h\h mutations and they can occur for many different\h reasons. The most simple mutations are point\h\h mutations. That is a change in just one base\h pair, from whichever base it was supposed to\h\h be to some other base. This can occur due to\h endogenous or exogenous mutagens. Carcinogens,\h\h UV light, or totally natural decay processes where\h radioactive nuclides within the body decay and\h\h produce a high energy particle that strikes a base\h in the genome of a particular cell. Errors can\h\h also occur during replication, where the enzyme\h creating the new strand makes a mistake. Repair\h\h enzymes exist to fix these errors, as well as the\h other mutations we described, but they don’t catch\h\h them all, so point mutations happen in every\h organism all the time. Most are neutral, many\h\h of the rest are harmful, and some are beneficial.\h It depends on whether any of the amino acids in\h\h the resulting protein change, and how that affects\h the function of that protein. If it’s an enzyme,\h\h it could function more efficiently. Or less.\h Or it could lose function. Or even change\h\h functions if several mutations accumulate. We have to understand some other types of\h\h mutations that can occur. There are mutations\h like insertions and deletions that change the\h\h reading frame of the gene, which usually result\h in a non-functional protein. But there are also\h\h macromutations. Very significant changes to\h the genome can sometimes occur. For example,\h\h gene duplication. During replication, the\h enzyme can copy a section of DNA more than\h\h once. Additionally, during crossing over\h between homologous chromosomes in meiosis,\h\h a type of cell division, misalignment can result\h in two copies of the same gene getting into one\h\h chromosome. With two copies of the same gene,\h neofunctionalization is now possible. One copy\h\h of the gene can be retained, while the other gene\h can slowly accumulate mutations and therefore\h\h yield a totally different protein product. No\h function is lost, while a new one can be gained,\h\h and studies show that around 50% of gene\h duplications lead to functional divergence.\h A similar situation occurs with orphan genes, or\h de novo genes. There are sections of DNA called\h\h promoters which sit next to the coding region\h of a gene that an enzyme will interact with,\h\h resulting in transcription of the gene. A mutation\h event can sometimes rearrange sections of the\h\h chromosome which result in a promoter being placed\h next to a previously non-coding section of DNA.\h\h This results in a brand new gene instantly, with\h a totally random sequence and therefore a totally\h\h random protein product. This protein might\h be useless, but it might not, and any modest\h\h functionality can be subsequently molded through\h natural selection. The potentiality of a process\h\h like gene duplication is magnified tremendously\h when entire chromosomes duplicate. This is again\h\h typically due to errors during cell division,\h where homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids\h\h don’t separate during meiosis so one cell ends up\h with multiple copies of the same chromosome. This\h\h leads to the possibility of many different\h genes going through neofunctionalization,\h\h which can have dramatic effects for an organism. Now if any of these mutations occur in the somatic\h\h cells of an organism, the effect is usually minor.\h But if they occur in the germline cells of the\h\h organism, or the cells that produce gametes,\h meaning sperm and eggs, then we are looking at\h\h the offspring having a significantly different\h genotype than the parents, and thus potentially\h\h a different phenotype, which refers to actual\h morphological differences. These are typically\h\h very tiny, but sometimes not so tiny. It simply\h depends on how those proteins influence embryonic\h\h development and the determination of the body\h plan. We have physically observed instances where\h\h even single point mutations can have drastic\h effects on an animal’s morphology, like legs\h\h growing from a fly’s head instead of antennae,\h extra pairs of wings, and other major changes.\h\h The implications for evolution are obvious. With this understood we can now begin to\h\h outline the various mechanisms by which evolution\h operates. Whereas Darwin envisioned only natural\h\h selection, over the 150 years since, we now know\h that there are many other mechanisms also at play.\h\h Apart from mutation, which produces genetic\h variety, and natural selection, where organisms\h\h better suited for survival and reproduction have\h their genes more likely to proliferate, there\h\h are a few other important ones. Genetic drift\h describes a change in the relative frequency of\h\h an allele in a population due to chance and random\h sampling. An allele is a copy of a gene. Most\h\h animals have two copies of every gene, one from\h each parent, and each copy is called an allele.\h\h Alleles can be dominant or recessive, and this\h genotype can dictate the phenotype, or the version\h\h of a particular trait that is expressed on the\h organism. There is also gene flow, which describes\h\h the movement of genes from one population to\h another, often due to migration, which can\h\h increase genetic diversity. Then there is sexual\h selection, or non-random mating based on perceived\h\h evolutionary fitness. This operates by criteria\h that are quite different from survivability, and\h\h can produce interesting morphological features.\h Horizontal gene transfer, niche construction,\h\h epigenetics, the list is long and we need\h not dwell on every detail for our purposes.\h As we can see, evolution relies largely on\h population dynamics, and changes that occur\h\h on the genetic level which Darwin could never\h have understood in his time, before we even\h\h knew that DNA existed. Creationists relentlessly\h talk about Darwinism and Darwinian evolution and\h\h in general never shut up about Darwin for this\h specific reason. He lived a long time ago before\h\h we actually understood evolution, so they will\h try to present evolution in this primitive lens.\h\h Young Earth creationists and intelligent design\h advocates alike will always return to the same\h\h mantra, random mutation and natural selection\h are insufficient in producing the variety of\h\h life. They will all say this every chance they\h get. And yet, even with the couple of minutes of\h\h background information we just went over, we can\h immediately see how dishonest this is. When they\h\h say random mutation, they mean point mutations.\h These are more limited in scope. They are ignoring\h\h macromutations like gene duplication, de\h novo genes, or chromosome duplication,\h\h which produce significant discrepancies\h in the genome in a single generation. And\h\h when they say natural selection, they are\h limiting evolution to a singular mechanism,\h\h ignoring the others we described. This is\h a deliberate misrepresentation of the scope\h\h and potentiality of evolutionary processes. More detailed attempts to misrepresent genetics\h\h will take advantage of the negative connotation of\h the word “mutation” to pretend that all mutations\h\h are harmful. They will say things like “mutations\h degrade genetic information”, as though a bucket\h\h of toxic green goo has fallen on the DNA and is\h giving it chemical burns. In reality mutations\h\h are simply changes to the genetic code. As we\h said, with point mutations, the vast majority\h\h are neutral. The mutation does not result in any\h change whatsoever to the protein product. Of the\h\h remaining possibilities, some are harmful and some\h are beneficial, we have to look at the change made\h\h to the protein. Is the amino acid that changed in\h the active site of an enzyme? Does this cause it\h\h to bind to its substrate more tightly? Or not at\h all? Any of these possibilities could be bad or\h\h good, depending on the situation. Significantly\h harmful mutations are not often observed because\h\h those organisms tend to die quickly without\h reproducing, so we disproportionately observe\h\h beneficial mutations and improved function, which\h can appear like design to the unprepared mind.\h Another creationist fixation has to do with\h probability. They will take any enzyme, like say\h\h DNA polymerase, and remark how unlikely it is for\h that to have arisen by chance. In order to make it\h\h seem impossible, they will play a devious numbers\h game. They’ll say: Here’s an enzyme with 300 amino\h\h acid residues, there are 20 amino acids, so the\h probability of this precise sequence evolving by\h\h chance is one in 20 to the 300th power. Their\h targets will gasp at the infinitesimal odds,\h\h and conclude that it can only exist because god\h willed it so. This is ridiculous. That precise\h\h sequence is far from the only sequence that will\h perform that function. Many of the amino acids\h\h in the active site of an enzyme have limited\h variability, although even those have some,\h\h but the rest of the amino acids contribute only\h to the overall shape of the enzyme, and thus have\h\h tremendous variability. There are sets of amino\h acids that are extremely similar. Amino acids\h\h have the same general structure plus a variable\h side chain. Here are a few that have an alkyl\h\h side chain, meaning they consist of only carbon\h and hydrogen. Anywhere we find one of these,\h\h we could easily swap to another similar one and\h the effect on the enzyme would be practically\h\h non-existent. Only if we switched from something\h like a hydrophobic to a hydrophilic side chain,\h\h like alkyl to one containing a hydroxyl group,\h could that potentially have an impact on the\h\h folding pattern, and even then it is unlikely to\h be significant. So we are saying that the majority\h\h of the amino acid residues could be completely\h different, and the function would be identical or\h\h similar. Furthermore, new enzymes don’t have to\h function optimally. They can perform a function\h\h with moderate efficiency and then get refined\h by natural selection over time. And finally,\h\h we know for a fact that many different\h sequences can perform the same function,\h\h because different organisms have different\h versions of the same enzymes. Looking again at\h\h DNA polymerase, different organisms have different\h polymerase enzymes. They have different sequences,\h\h and we give them different names, yet they\h all copy DNA. With genetic engineering we\h\h manipulate the amino acid sequence of enzymes\h to make them perform more efficiently than\h\h the natural counterpart. There is tremendous\h variability and nothing is perfect in the first\h\h place. So this is lazy propaganda on the part\h of creationists. Nature creates many sequences,\h\h stumbles upon functional sequences by chance,\h and those are optimized and amplified by natural\h\h selection. Plenty of research has been done\h which corroborates the fact that totally random\h\h sequences are an abundant source of bioactive\h RNA and peptides. This is not controversial.\h Recalling the creationist claim that\h microevolution is possible but not macroevolution,\h\h this seems even more ridiculous in the light\h of molecular biology. There is no mechanistic\h\h distinction between the two, it’s all based on\h mutations. We already explained how certain point\h\h mutations and especially macromutations can\h produce significant morphological change even\h\h in a single generation. Changes to HOX and\h TALE genes can dramatically revise the body\h\h plan. Differential gene activation can affect cell\h differentiation, thus allowing cells in different\h\h regions of the body to do different things. And\h in general, all of this hinges on creationist\h\h incredulity regarding embryonic development.\h Creationists have no idea how this process\h\h works. If a creationist tells you that evolution\h can’t produce large scale changes to a body plan,\h\h ask them how a body plan is implemented during\h embryonic development in the first place. Just\h\h ask them point blank. All animals begin as one\h cell, right? So how does that become a specific\h\h animal with a specific body plan? Just sit and\h wait for an answer. If they offer anything at all,\h\h it will be vague, like: “The DNA has the\h instructions and that’s how you get the body\h\h plan.” But how? Ask specifically and repeatedly.\h How, mechanistically, on the molecular level,\h\h does the body plan develop? I bet you a million\h dollars that not a single creationist will give\h\h you a detailed answer. The reaction to this is\h therefore: You have no idea how the body plan\h\h arises. You have no idea what happens on the\h cellular or molecular level as a single cell\h\h becomes a complete organism. Yet you are somehow\h an expert on what this process can and can’t\h\h produce? Hopefully this will embarrass them enough\h to do some learning, or at least question their\h\h beliefs. If they are quiet enough to receive more\h information, you can then tell them about how body\h\h plans arise from the time-regulated expression\h of specific genes, so mutations in those genes\h\h can change the body plan. Tell them about all the\h kinds of macromutations they definitely have never\h\h heard of. Tell them about examples of visible\h change that result from even point mutations,\h\h like flies growing legs instead of antennae.\h Creationists do not know these things. There\h\h is no barrier preventing new species from\h emerging. Mutations accumulate and the organisms\h\h change accordingly, so there is no meaningful\h distinction between micro and macroevolution.\h Getting more specific on the anatomical\h level, looking at certain transitions,\h\h like from sea to land or from land to sea, is it\h really that shocking to go from hands and feet,\h\h to webbed hands and feet, to fins? Is it really\h that hard to wrap one’s head around how that might\h\h occur? What are the necessary changes to the\h genome that can push animal morphology in that\h\h direction? Even with humans, early in embryonic\h development, hands and feet form in flipper-like\h\h paddle shapes. Fingers and toes subsequently\h separate, elongate, and then lose webbing that\h\h is between them. This loss of webbing is due\h to interdigital necrosis, a type of cell death,\h\h so genes are selectively expressed in those\h cells that result in those cells dying such that\h\h the fingers can separate. If those genes are not\h expressed, the webbing can remain, and there are\h\h disorders in humans where precisely this happens.\h If this occurred with animals in aquatic habitats,\h\h it would be an enormous fitness benefit.\h It’s a heritable trait, so all of a sudden\h\h many organisms within a population can have\h webbed extremities. Further modification to\h\h the genome can affect embryonic limb development\h such that a more fin-like structure is retained,\h\h and then you have fins. All of this is determined\h during embryonic development, where the limbs are\h\h going through different stages anyway. Large scale\h morphological change can occur simply by silencing\h\h a certain aspect of embryonic development in a\h particular part of the body. It’s as simple as\h\h blocking a single gene from being expressed. And\h by looking at this example of webbed extremities,\h\h we are even identifying intermediary structures.\h Life wouldn’t have to go straight to fins. There\h\h can be many gradations in between, such as\h hybrid structures that are not optimized\h\h for either walking or swimming. Even this\h kind of anatomy can be considered useful,\h\h because such an organism can suddenly evade\h predators in either habitat, land or sea.\h Continuing with embryonic development, a favorite\h creationist talking point is to reference the\h\h early history of embryology. In the 19th century,\h Ernst Haeckel pioneered this field by observing\h\h the embryos of many different species and\h hand-drawing their development at various stages.\h\h Comparing these developmental pathways offers\h many clues regarding evolutionary relationships,\h\h since many aspects of development are shared\h between distantly related animals. For example,\h\h all chordates, including mammals, birds, reptiles,\h amphibians, fish, tunicates, and lancelets, have a\h\h notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal\h arches, a post-anal tail, and an endostyle or\h\h thyroid gland at some point in their development.\h Some chordates have all of these characteristics\h\h as adults, like lancelets, but others lose at\h least some of them later on. For example, humans\h\h lack an intact notochord, pharyngeal arches, and\h post-anal tail. Our notochord gets broken up to\h\h become the intervertebral discs, the pharyngeal\h arches become parts of our face and neck,\h\h and the post-anal tail shrinks away to a tiny\h vestige of its former self. But these structures\h\h still do form during embryonic development. We\h have 10-12 tail vertebrae before they retract\h\h into the soft tissue. It would seem odd from\h the perspective of design that embryos would\h\h go through stages where structures grow that\h will not be present on the mature organism.\h\h But it makes perfect sense in the context of\h evolution, where development begins a certain way,\h\h and then mutations cause gene expression to\h change at a particular stage, where existing\h\h structures then become reduced or modified. What Haeckel correctly showed was that all\h\h chordates go through a phylotypic or pharyngula\h stage, where the embryos of animals as diverse\h\h as elephants and sharks look extremely\h similar. What he got wrong was an idea\h\h he referred to as “ontogeny recapitulates\h phylogeny”, or the idea that organisms\h\h recapitulate their evolutionary ancestry during\h development. There is some truth to this notion,\h\h like the way that mammalian earbones detach from\h the jaw during development, but broadly speaking\h\h the idea is not accurate. By this we mean that a\h mammal doesn’t go through a specific fish stage,\h\h followed by an amphibian stage, and then a\h reptile stage, and so forth. Later embryologists\h\h recognized the extreme similarity early on but\h that embryos then diverge radically in morphology.\h The drama enters when people accuse Haeckel of\h fraudulence. While this is primarily creationists,\h\h it also included a few biologists. They will\h say that he fudged the scale or exaggerated\h\h characteristics, since they were hand drawings.\h In reality he made them the same size for ease\h\h of comparison. Additionally he accidentally\h used the same drawing for three embryos in\h\h his first edition, but this was pointed out to\h him and he fixed the images for later editions.\h\h Creationists essentially make a lot of fuss out\h of nothing, and when they bring this up you can\h\h ask them to clarify what they mean and where they\h got their information. They will have no response.\h\h Even more important, however, is the fact that\h Haeckel was undeniably correct. Embryos do go\h\h through these stages, and various mammalian\h embryos are virtually indistinguishable for a\h\h significant portion of development, something\h that is easily confirmed in the modern era\h\h where we no longer have to draw embryos, we can\h easily get real-time images of them. They look\h\h more or less just like Haeckel’s drawings. Moving on, there are some classic arguments\h\h from intelligent design proponents that must be\h neutralized. The first is the so-called waiting\h\h time problem. This one says that adaptations which\h require multiple mutations are impossible because\h\h of the improbability of those specific mutations\h occurring in a reasonable time span. There are\h\h a lot of issues here. First, nature is never\h going for a specific set of mutations. Mutations\h\h occur and they are either selected for or they\h aren’t. And these mutations do not have to occur\h\h in a specific sequence, they could occur in any\h sequence across an entire population and then come\h\h together during the recombination phase of sexual\h reproduction, such that each parent can have one\h\h mutation and the offspring has both. Furthermore,\h the idea that each individual mutation can’t be\h\h selected for because only the entire set confers\h the beneficial adaptation is incorrect. Individual\h\h mutations could still confer a slight survival\h advantage and therefore proliferate statistically.\h A similar argument from ID proponents is that\h of irreducible complexity. This states that some\h\h biological structures are so complex, with so many\h interconnected parts, that it can’t possibly have\h\h evolved, because removing just one component\h renders the structure unusable, and therefore\h\h none of the individual components can have been\h selected for, such that it could have arisen\h\h piecemeal. It’s all or nothing. Their favorite\h example of such a structure is the bacterial\h\h flagellum. They will describe this structure\h using as much mechanical language as possible,\h\h drawing parallels to actual human machinery.\h This is part of the deception. Humans built\h\h these things, so god must have built this thing.\h In actuality, this is a façade. First of all,\h\h when describing something like the bacterial\h flagellum, they are never honest about how many\h\h different types of bacterial flagella there are,\h and the wide range of complexity they display,\h\h which demonstrate the range of solutions nature\h can invent to solve the same problem. Just because\h\h a flagellum is highly complex now, it doesn’t mean\h it was always that way. Individual components can\h\h have complexified after the general function was\h reached, and there are extant flagella which lack\h\h components that others possess, yet they still\h function. Second, they always ignore the concept\h\h of exaptation. Instead of waiting for entirely\h new proteins to arise, like those that become the\h\h components of a bacterial flagellum, existing\h proteins can be slightly modified to develop\h\h entirely new functions. Sometimes a very small\h number of mutations is enough to achieve this,\h\h and a new protein suddenly exists for inclusion\h in some apparatus. Third, any such irreducible\h\h structures are never actually irreducible, and\h often times reduced structures specifically\h\h do exist. For the bacterial flagellum, a\h corresponding reduced structure is called the\h\h injectisome. This is a needle-like protein complex\h that uses components of the flagellar apparatus,\h\h but instead of generating motion it secretes\h effector proteins. It doesn’t matter whether\h\h the flagellum evolved from the injectisome or vice\h versa, the claim that ID proponents make is that\h\h with any irreducibly complex apparatus, there is\h no possibility of any reduced structure. Yet here\h\h we see one. It uses only some of the components\h of the flagellum and serves a totally different\h\h function. We can say the same thing about\h absolutely any molecular or anatomical feature\h\h that they claim is irreducibly complex. When they\h bring up eyesight, they ignore everything we know\h\h about the evolution of eyes, and the many types\h of eyes in the animal kingdom, ranging from a\h\h tiny bundle of photoreceptors to complex eyeballs\h like those in humans or squids, and everything\h\h in between. In fact it is known that eyes have\h evolved independently dozens of times in different\h\h species, as an example of convergent evolution.\h Vision is a highly valuable trait, so any features\h\h that bestow this function will be heavily selected\h for, which is why it happened so many times,\h\h resulting in many different types of eyes. It’s\h not necessary for entire eyes to suddenly exist,\h\h smaller structures are still useful and\h can be selected for. Even a naked bundle\h\h of photoreceptors can indicate to an organism\h which direction light is coming from. That’s\h\h enough for it to move towards a region where it\h can do photosynthesis, or feed on photosynthetic\h\h microorganisms. The same can be said for metabolic\h pathways. They will claim that the Krebs cycle is\h\h irreducibly complex, but the evolution of this\h cycle is well-understood, utilizing these same\h\h concepts of sequential changes and exaptation\h of existing proteins. They simply ignore the\h\h mountains of primary literature on these topics,\h knowing their targets will never read it either.\h A good analogy for irreducible complexity is\h complex ecosystems. These are comprised of\h\h many different species of animals, plants, fungi,\h and microorganisms. There is a delicate balance,\h\h such that the removal of one species\h could cause the whole thing to collapse,\h\h just like one protein from the flagellum. But\h this doesn’t mean it was poofed into existence\h\h precisely as it is today. Ecosystems respond to\h the stimuli that are present, minor perturbations,\h\h slowly shifting inputs, and interdependence can\h emerge gradually. Tiny changes over long periods\h\h of time allow for a gradual response that produces\h a more robust system. A sudden dramatic change,\h\h like deleting an entire population of organisms,\h has a much bigger impact. That we can’t start\h\h stripping away components of the ecosystem doesn’t\h mean that simpler ecosystems can’t exist, or that\h\h this specific ecosystem wasn’t at one point much\h simpler. The same goes for any cellular component.\h In general, the pseudoscientific nature of\h intelligent design can be exposed simply by asking\h\h its proponents to put forward a rigorous model.\h Which biological structures are designed? Which\h\h are not? Is there an empirical way to test whether\h something is designed? Can they make predictions\h\h of any kind regarding biological systems? Intelligent design is just a god of\h\h the gaps argument in a tuxedo, nothing more. Another aspect of genetics that creationists\h\h lie about is the proportion of the genome that is\h functional. Genes themselves make up around 1-2%\h\h of the genome, that is the percentage of actual\h coding DNA, whether protein-coding, or genes for\h\h ribosomes, transfer RNA, and so forth. Some time\h ago it was thought that the rest served little to\h\h no function, and was therefore referred to as junk\h DNA. Over the decades we have come to understand\h\h that there are sections that serve some role in\h influencing gene expression. There are promoters,\h\h enhancers, and other elements that have important\h functions. But this still puts the cap at around\h\h 10% in terms of the proportion of the genome that\h is functional. The rest remains junk DNA. This\h\h of course makes perfect sense in the context of\h evolution, as nature uses a large genetic canvas,\h\h and only certain portions of the genome evolve\h functionality by chance, while the rest must still\h\h be replicated and maintained at great energetic\h cost. Nature is not so efficient that it could\h\h have evolved genomes that are entirely functional,\h and the percentage of DNA that is functional\h\h decreases along with decreasing population sizes,\h since the greater the population, the greater the\h\h strength of natural selection on mutations.\h So many eukaryotes are able to accrue lots of\h\h junk DNA, as opposed to some bacterial species\h that comparatively have a larger proportion of\h\h functional DNA in their genomes. In the context of\h design this does not make any sense. Why couldn’t\h\h a designer simply design a genome without\h wasting so much space? Why include the 90%\h\h that doesn’t do anything? It is simply that a\h\h small fraction turned out to have functions that\h are now well-understood by molecular biologists.\h Speaking of promoters and other genomic elements,\h plenty of research has been done surrounding these\h\h structures that specifically demonstrates how\h resourceful nature can be. Scientists have taken\h\h a wild-type strain of E. coli and stripped away\h the native promoter region of the lac operon,\h\h the gene necessary for metabolizing lactose.\h This is a segment of about 100 base pairs,\h\h which was replaced with totally random sequences,\h such that the gene will not be transcribed and\h\h the resulting lactose-metabolizing enzyme\h cannot form. As a control, in one case,\h\h the promoter region was simply deleted and\h not replaced with anything. Needless to say,\h\h these bacteria could not survive on lactose alone\h because they could not metabolize it. Different\h\h clones with different random sequences were\h grown on a medium consisting of some glycerol,\h\h which they could metabolize, and increasing levels\h of lactose. After a few rounds of mutation and\h\h selection, clones arose which metabolized lactose.\h After about 100 rounds, these new E. coli clones\h\h thrived on lactose alone and the newly evolved\h promoters functioned as well as the wild type,\h\h some of which were also paired with mutations in\h the gene itself and thus different proteins. The\h\h only one that could never evolve was the one where\h the promoter region had simply been stripped away.\h\h This illustrates again the power of selection in\h vivo, showing how random sequences can acquire\h\h function in the presence of a selection mechanism,\h something creationists will forever deny even when\h\h it is demonstrated for them clear as day. It\h also demonstrates another fact creationists\h\h always forget to mention, that there are many\h solutions to a problem, which means completely\h\h distinct proteins can perform the same function\h to a satisfactory extent, something which makes\h\h their big number games even more meaningless. Another creationist claim in the area of\h\h molecular biology pertains to soft\h tissue found in dinosaur bones. The process\h by which soft tissue decays depends on contact\h\h with air and water. But this soft tissue was in\h the dry interior of the specimen, stabilized by\h\h contact with hemoglobin and the mineral walls\h of the surrounding pores. Though fascinating,\h\h it does not change the dating of the specimen. In general, out of everything we could summarize\h\h regarding genetics and molecular biology, and how\h these fields corroborate evolutionary principles\h\h far beyond reasonable doubt, we certainly can\h focus on mutations, embryonic development,\h\h and other such complex topics. But we also can\h simply point to heredity. This is something\h\h most people can wrap their heads around. Your\h genome is very similar to those of your parents,\h\h because it is a combination of the genomes of\h your parents. That’s how paternity tests work,\h\h on the basis of genetic similarity. Using the\h principle of genetic similarity, we can tell\h\h who your father is, and your father’s father, and\h his father before him, and so forth. So why would\h\h anyone presume that this concept doesn’t work more\h broadly for genetic similarity between species?\h\h Humans and chimpanzees share 98.8% of their\h genome. This indicates very recent common\h\h ancestry. Other primates are slightly more\h dissimilar so the divergence was slightly more\h\h distant. We already discussed orphan genes,\h\h or de novo genes. When an organism develops an\h entirely new gene, that gene will continue to\h\h show up in its entire pool of descendants if the\h organism is reproductively successful. This is when a retrovirus, a special\h kind of virus that is capable of inserting\h\h its own genetic code into the genome of a host\h cell, does precisely this in a germline cell of\h\h an animal. Its offspring will then have that\h unique section of what was the viral genome,\h\h and this will be another marker we can use to\h identify common ancestry. There are countless\h\h ways to confirm evolutionary lineages that make\h no sense whatsoever in the context of design.\h We can expand this way of thinking to any genome\h as a whole. In part one of this series, we examined\h some of the claims that creationists make\h\h regarding cosmology and planetary science. Chemistry is rather limited in space,\h\h since it works much better in a confined\h volume, typically a liquid solution,\h\h like an aqueous solution. Additionally, there are plenty of pathways to get\h\h these molecules on a prebiotic Earth. The famous\h Miller-Urey experiment from the 1950s took simple\h\h molecules like methane and ammonia, introduced a\h spark, and got amino acids. The takeaway from all\h\h of this is that it is no problem to get amino\h acids. It can be taken for granted that amino\h\h acids were abundant on a prebiotic Earth. To speak\h a bit further about the Miller-Urey experiment,\h\h this is referenced excessively by both\h creationists and science advocates. The\h\h danger for science advocates is to pretend that\h the experiment substantiated abiogenesis, when it\h\h really did not. It produced the most simple and\h tiny building blocks of life, which was a great\h\h achievement, but is not even remotely comparable\h to producing life. In shallow areas like\h\h tidal pools and hot springs, there are natural\h cycles like day and night, as well as tides,\h\h which result in sequential polymerization\h and degradation. As a pool dries out,\h\h a chain lengthens. Once wet again there is some\h dissociation and new monomers can migrate to the\h\h growing chain within solution. That’s right, humans are apes. The common\h ancestor of apes and monkeys was farther back,\h\h around 25 to 30 million years ago.
