So expecting evolution\h to allow an organism on one branch to jump to\h\h some other branch is totally nonsensical. Nature\h doesn’t do that. Furthermore, evolution is not\h\h some set plan with certain goals in mind. Nature\h didn’t intend to produce any particular species,\h\h nor would the exact same thing occur today given\h the same population of ancestors. So asking why\h\h some evolutionary lineage from the past doesn’t\h continue to occur today doesn’t make any sense,\h\h particularly as those more basal species\h don’t exist any longer, and in the case of\h\h monkeys producing humans, it never happened in the\h first place. That’s what makes this question so\h\h hilarious. Beyond the absurdity of thinking that\h modern monkeys are somehow the direct ancestors\h\h of humans, it’s the idea of evolution being\h some mandatory gate that funnels every single\h\h organism of a species up to the next level of some\h intended and pre-determined evolutionary pathway.\h\h In reality, small changes occur within populations\h of organisms, and subpopulations then diverge,\h\h creating two different branches\h which then develop independently.\h It should be noted that when creationists are\h skeptical about certain events we outlined\h\h a moment ago, you can point them to modern\h observations that corroborate all of these\h\h steps. Endosymbiosis is not merely hypothetical,\h it has been reproduced in the lab. An algal cell\h\h engulfed a bacterial cell with the capability of\h metabolizing atmospheric nitrogen, and this became\h\h an organelle of the larger cell, which we call a\h nitroplast. The emergence of multicellularity has\h\h also been observed, with a unicellular algal\h species evolving multicellularity under\h\h observation. These processes are not speculative,\h they are well-substantiated. The grand scale of\h\h all these lineages is instead corroborated by the\h fossil record, which we will get to a bit later.\h While different types of creationists have\h different opinions on evolution, Young Earth\h\h creationists reject the entire concept of common\h descent. They believe all species were created\h\h more or less precisely as they are, and they\h believe that they were brought two by two onto a\h\h huge ark by Noah to survive a global flood, after\h which they proliferated to yield all the animals\h\h we see today. This notion is so profoundly absurd\h it’s difficult to even know where to begin. First,\h\h as we mentioned, the perception of the animal\h kingdom this requires is infantile. There are\h\h not merely a few dozen animal species. It’s not\h lions and elephants and a few others and that’s\h\h it. There are millions of animal species, perhaps\h even tens of millions. The sheer biomass that\h\h would be present on the ark would require it to be\h substantially larger than any ship ever built even\h\h in modern times. And that’s just to physically\h fit the animals on board in a compact manner.\h\h Then what would happen? What would they eat? The\h mass of food required would be far greater than\h\h the biomass of the animals, requiring the ark\h to be even an order of magnitude larger still,\h\h especially if we want to actually separate the\h animals so they don’t eat or murder each other.\h Some creationists try to solve this problem by\h claiming there were far fewer types of animals at\h\h the time of the flood. So instead of thousands\h of species of beetles, there was just one,\h\h and the diversity of beetles we see today was\h produced from that point forward. The same\h\h would go for the variety of feline species,\h that lions and tigers and cheetahs and pumas\h\h and ocelots and jaguars and housecats all diverged\h after the flood when animals began to repopulate.\h\h And the same for mice and rats and hamsters\h and gerbils, and so forth. This is even more\h\h ridiculous than the idea of millions of species\h on one boat. These creationists refuse to believe\h\h in gradual evolution over millions of years, but\h they will believe in ultra-rapid evolution over\h\h a few hundred years? Many of these animals were\h known in antiquity, so the diversification had\h\h to be almost instantaneous. So creationists adopt\h an exaggerated and physically impossible version\h\h of the process they are specifically denying in\h order to cling to this ridiculous myth of the ark.\h Regardless of which version one adopts, there\h are many more absurdities that arise once the\h\h flood is over. How did the two penguins get all\h the way to Antarctica? How did the kangaroos get\h\h to Australia? How did all of the animals get\h to their ecological niches, leaving no trace\h\h of themselves anywhere else? What about all the\h plants? Most of them would die in a global flood,\h\h yet they’re everywhere. What about freshwater\h aquatic life? That would all die out as soon\h\h as their habitats mixed with salty ocean water.\h Furthermore, two organisms of each species do\h\h not have enough genetic diversity to produce\h large, healthy populations, so how does that\h\h work? Both for animals and for humans, who\h supposedly descended from one man and one\h\h woman not once but twice. And the list goes on. The most common response to all of these issues\h\h is typically magic. How did all the animals find\h the ark and then get back to their habitats after\h\h the flood? Magic. How did Noah prevent them\h from eating each other on the ark? Magic. How\h\h were their progeny not cripplingly inbred?\h Magic. When you believe in a magic deity,\h\h it is acceptable to propose magic as a solution to\h any problem. In such a case the only recourse is\h\h to remind creationists at every opportunity\h possible that they are believing in magic.\h Let’s now pivot to paleontology and the fossil\h record, because this is the primary line of\h\h evidence that substantiates everything we are\h describing. All of these lineages on the tree of\h\h life are immaculately supported by the millions\h of fossilized specimens that have been found,\h\h which can be accurately dated to specific time\h periods and which populate all of these branches,\h\h thus elucidating the forms which have existed in\h the past, as well as their gradual morphological\h\h change. Of course the fossil record is\h not perfect, because fossilization is a\h\h relatively rare occurrence. We will never have\h fossils for every single species that has ever\h\h existed. But if we are doing a very large jigsaw\h puzzle, we will be able to tell what the picture\h\h is without every single last puzzle piece. First of all, what is a fossil? A fossil is\h\h the preserved remains of an organism or some kind\h of evidence of its behavior that is found in rock,\h\h soil, or amber, that is over 10,000\h years old. These can be very large,\h\h if preserving a large animal, or they can be very\h small, preserving even microorganisms. The reason\h\h these are rare is that dead organisms tend to\h decay very quickly, so this kind of preservation\h\h occurs during relatively uncommon events. The\h organism must be rapidly covered by sediment,\h\h so it might become buried by the sea floor, or\h lava, or tar. Once trapped within sediment, the\h\h body does decay, but bodily particles get replaced\h by minerals, especially in hard parts like bones,\h\h teeth, or shells. Once the organism is gone, its\h precise form remains preserved for us to find,\h\h so we can gather highly detailed information\h about their morphologies, and more. This is the\h\h most common type of fossilization and it works\h well with bony animals, but other processes\h\h can also occur, like insects getting trapped in\h resin or amber. This is one way that we can find\h\h the remains of soft-bodied organisms that don’t\h fossilize well. There are also trace fossils,\h\h which unlike the body fossils we just described,\h preserve the behavior of organisms. This would\h\h include things like footprints or burrows.\h Paleontologists study all of these fossils\h\h to learn about what kinds of living organisms\h lived, and when. Finding remains of aquatic\h\h animals in the middle of a desert tells us there\h was once water there, and so forth. And there are\h\h numerous methods of dating fossils, including\h radiometric dating as most are aware, but also\h\h electron spin resonance, thermoluminescence,\h and others. There is nothing speculative about\h\h the dates that we assign to fossilized remains. Creationists have many issues with fossilization,\h\h of course. First, they pretend fossilization\h should be impossible because geological processes\h\h are so slow. This is ironic, considering the\h lightning fast rates of sediment deposition\h\h they pretend are possible for the generation\h of post-flood geological structures. But\h\h nevertheless, as slow as sediment deposition\h typically is, other processes can be very fast.\h\h Rivers can flood suddenly. Tidal waves can occur.\h Volcanoes erupt. There are many violent processes\h\h that can rapidly bury organisms. These are not a\h daily occurrence, but over hundreds of millions\h\h of years, there are plenty of opportunities for\h burial and later fossilization by these means.\h\h Additionally, there are even slow methods of\h fossilization. Animals decay because of bacteria,\h\h but there are swampy anoxic regions where bacteria\h that decay organisms can’t survive, so animals can\h\h be slowly preserved as they are buried by sediment\h at a more typical rate. The same can be said\h\h for deoxygenated ocean basins, where decaying\h bacteria and larger scavengers can’t survive.\h Then of course the biggest problem is that\h creationists are in complete denial as to\h\h the extent of the fossil record. Way back in\h Darwin’s time we didn’t have a lot to work\h\h with. That’s why he explicitly stated that\h the success of his theory would hinge on\h\h whether paleontological evidence of transitional\h forms would be discovered. Over 150 years later,\h\h we have plenty to work with. The number\h and variety of specimens we have found is\h\h staggering. To present an exhaustive list of\h transitional species would require an entire\h\h series of videos unto itself, so we will not do\h that, but simply googling “list of transitional\h\h species” is enough to keep one occupied for\h days. Rather, we can highlight a handful of\h\h important ones to illustrate precisely why these\h specimens so remarkably substantiate evolution.\h\h Look at Ambulocetus. This is an early amphibious\h cetacean from a little under 50 million years ago,\h\h so this is along the lineage that produced modern\h whales. The transitional nature of its morphology\h\h is immaculate. It was able to walk on land roughly\h like a sea lion, and it swam somewhat like an\h\h otter, using its limbs as well as undulation for\h propulsion. It did not have a tail like whales do,\h\h but it may have had webbed feet. This is where\h Ambulocetus sits on the family tree in comparison\h\h to modern whales. And of course there are many\h other transitional species along this lineage\h\h ending with whales that we could look at, such as\h Basilosaurus, from around 40 million years ago.\h\h This is quite different from Ambulocetus, being\h that it was an early marine mammal, and it was\h\h fully aquatic. But we still see the intermediate\h morphological features that would lead to whales.\h We should make one thing clear at this point. In\h a certain sense, every species is a transitional\h\h species. There are no evolutionary dead ends apart\h from mass extinctions. Life is always changing.\h\h Some organisms fit an environmental niche\h extremely well, so if that environment changes\h\h very little, then certain forms can persist with\h very little change, such as with sharks. Shark\h\h diversity has grown incredibly over hundreds\h of millions of years, but there are certain\h\h sharks today which are very similar to ancient\h sharks, although smaller. But for the most part,\h\h change is always occurring. We say transitional\h species when referring to extinct species present\h\h on lineages that produced extant species. This is\h the difference between what paleontologists refer\h\h to as stem groups and crown groups. A crown group\h includes the most recent common ancestor of all\h\h the currently living members of a group plus all\h its descendants. A stem group includes exclusively\h\h extinct species that existed prior to the crown\h group and which do not share all the features of\h\h the crown group. There are species that are alive\h today that will one day be extinct, and they may\h\h at that point be considered transitional species\h from the perspective of scientists in that time.\h\h It is not the case that there are certain,\h special, perfect forms that are somehow the\h\h goal of evolution, and inferior species that\h have to be traversed to get from one perfect\h\h form to another. It’s just what has existed in\h the past and what exists today. Ambulocetus is\h\h not inherently inferior to modern whales, there\h are many factors that go into extinctions,\h\h and one day whales will go extinct as well.\h But we can use the fossil record to understand\h\h how it is related to other mammals, and\h other animals in general. It is the case\h\h that the closest living relatives of whales are\h hippos. This does not mean hippos are ancestors\h\h of whales. It means that hippos and whales share\h a common ancestor that is more recent than the\h\h common ancestor of both hippos and whales with\h other mammals. Going backwards on the branches\h\h that led to hippos and whales would show us an\h ancestor with a totally different morphology,\h\h and distinct populations of this species produced\h different branches which diverged dramatically\h\h over tens of millions of years. This is one of the\h main concepts that creationists do not understand,\h\h and need to be taught with clarity. Those who resist this information use a\h\h number of tactics. First, they will simply deny\h the existence of transitional species. They can\h\h do this in a dishonest way by discussing the time\h of Darwin. They will exclaim that Darwin admitted\h\h that the fossil record posed a huge challenge\h for his evolutionary theory, because he did\h\h not see sufficient transitional species. And this\h is true of the 1860s. It is no longer true today,\h\h not by a longshot. For those who dare to\h examine this from a modern perspective,\h\h no matter what types of specimens are collected,\h or how many, they will refuse to accept them as\h\h being truly transitional. They will pretend that\h any fossilized organism must have been a version\h\h of what exists today. This means they will insist\h that there are no transitional species between\h\h land mammals and whales, no matter how ignorant\h this proclamation is regarding the anatomy of\h\h the organism. Similarly, all hominid remains are\h either chimps or humans. All Australophithecines,\h\h all Homo species, they’re all either a chimp or a\h human, no matter how inconsistent that assignment\h\h is with the specimens, which very clearly display\h intermediate morphologies, with some more basal\h\h characteristics, like longer arms, and some\h modern characteristics, like bipedalism. It\h\h doesn’t matter that every single biological\h anthropologist in the world would attest to\h\h the absurdity of this claim, creationists will\h deny the existence of these distinct species.\h In this particular realm of hominid evolution,\h there are a few tropes that creationists bring\h\h up all the time, so let’s go through them\h briefly. First, they are obsessed with Lucy,\h\h the first substantial specimen ever found of\h Australopithecus afarensis. It was about 40%\h\h complete, and allowed us to prove that these apes\h were bipedal, due to some very clear anatomical\h\h characteristics pertaining to the skull, pelvis,\h and knees. But\h they will try to poke holes in Lucy and pretend\h\h she was a chimp in order to discredit hominid\h evolution. They will also say that there was a\h\h baboon bone found in the specimen, so it’s just\h a baboon. It’s actually true, decades later it\h\h was determined that one of the bones belonged\h to a baboon, not to Lucy. This means nothing\h\h beyond that. One of the bones did not belong to\h Lucy, the bipedal Australopithecine, but rather\h\h to a baboon. That’s the end of the story. They will often bring up the Nebraska man.\h\h This was the name given to a putative hominid\h species based on a tooth that was found in 1917.\h\h By 1922 it was realized by the scientific\h community that it actually belonged to an\h\h extinct peccary species, which had been severely\h weathered such that it resembled a hominid tooth.\h\h This was a misidentification made by a singular\h paleontologist who specifically warned that it\h\h was not definitive proof of a hominid, but\h creationists pretend this singular mistake\h\h somehow invalidates all the hundreds of\h hominid specimens that are clear as day.\h They will also bring up the Piltdown man. This was\h a paleoanthropological fraud where bone fragments\h\h were presented by an amateur archeologist as\h belonging to an early hominid species. They were\h\h accepted for a while in Britain, but debunked just\h a few years later by the wider anthropological\h\h community. Creationists again use this singular\h incident to try to deny the entire field of\h\h biological anthropology, neglecting to acknowledge\h that it is simply an instance of fraud that was\h\h exposed by the scientific community itself.\h In the end, this is all creationists can do,\h\h make a fuss over nothing to deflect from an\h entire field of science they don’t want to exist,\h\h because we have firmly substantiated dozens of\h hominid species between modern humans and our\h\h most recent common ancestor with other apes,\h and there is not a single honest and educated\h\h person in the anthropological community who\h would pretend that all of them are somehow\h\h just chimps or people, due to the undeniable\h intermediary characteristics they possess.\h Another thing creationists do is they fixate\h on remaining gaps in the fossil record. This\h\h is for two reasons. First, they know, just\h as paleontologists do, that the fossil\h\h record will never be 100% complete. It is not\h likely that every single species was fossilized,\h\h and it is even less likely that we would find\h them all. They’re hard to find. That does not\h\h prevent us from filling in the fossil record\h thoroughly enough to make evolution and common\h\h descent consistent beyond reasonable doubt, just\h on the grounds of the fossil record alone. The\h\h other reason they do this is to use numbers in\h a tricky way. Let’s say there are two organisms,\h\h A and B, and the transition between them is a\h mystery. There is a gap in the fossil record.\h\h Then we find organism C, which immaculately fits\h the description of a transitional species between\h\h A and B. But what’s this! Things just keep getting\h\h worse and worse. Of course this is preposterous,\h filling in gaps like this corroborates an\h\h evolutionary lineage, and in the limit of hundreds\h of transitional species, the morphological gaps\h\h become smaller and smaller, such that to doubt\h their representation of an evolutionary lineage\h\h becomes more and more unreasonable. But\h creationists are not reasonable, so this is\h\h the game they play. An example is the transition\h from dinosaurs to modern birds. Archeopteryx was\h\h discovered way back in 1861, and presented as a\h feathered dinosaur along a lineage from raptors to\h\h birds. This was not enough for creationists, which\h is fair enough, but since then, countless other\h\h forms have been found more clearly outlining this\h lineage from two-legged dinosaurs to modern birds.\h\h The gradual change in morphology that can be seen\h is quite striking, and in fact, if one stares at\h\h an ostrich for long enough, the resemblance\h to dinosaurs like raptors is actually quite\h\h obvious. The real difference is the feathers,\h which evolved very easily from dermal placodes\h\h in a manner similar to scales, as they are\h both made of keratin. In fact, there is a point\h\h mutation that can occur in certain chickens that\h causes them to grow feathers instead of scales\h\h on their legs and feet, which makes them look\h pretty funny. Additionally, ectopic expression\h\h of the regulatory genes Spry2 and β-catenin\h in embryonic alligator skin produces bud-like\h\h structures that resemble avian long feather\h buds. These are just examples of how trivial\h\h it is to explain these types of changes, like\h scaly dinosaurs producing feathered birds. But\h\h we will discuss genetics in the next installment. Looking further at the fossil record as a whole,\h\h it presents enormous problems for creationists\h of all varieties. First, for those who believe\h\h that these specimens were deposited rapidly\h during sedimentation after a global flood,\h\h things get absurd very quickly. Of course these\h are dead organisms that were not on the ark,\h\h so they were all alive at the same time, died\h at the same time, and were deposited at the\h\h same time. The idea that all of these organisms\h were deposited into specific layers so flawlessly\h\h becomes a statistical impossibility.\h With regard to the Phanerozoic Eon,\h\h trilobites are present exclusively in the deepest\h layers and no others. Dinosaurs are in the middle\h\h layers and no others. Hominid remains are in the\h top layers and no others. Every type of organism\h\h is present in a narrow range of strata, which\h just happens to delineate gradual morphological\h\h change from basal forms to modern forms. Creationists make transparently desperate\h\h attempts to explain the distribution.\h One such idea is hydraulic sorting.\h\h They pretend the fossils are organized according\h to physical features like mass and buoyancy. This\h\h is ridiculous, as there is simply no correlation.\h Ammonites are very light and buoyant but they are\h\h present only in the bottom layers, because\h they are so ancient. Turtles are dense but\h\h are in the middle to higher layers. We can also\h look to discrepancies within forms. Trilobites\h\h come in a wide variety of sizes. Shouldn’t they\h therefore be spread out amongst the layers? But\h\h they’re all at the bottom. There is no physical\h characteristic that can possibly determine how\h\h these fossils were deposited simultaneously\h into very specific layers all around the world.\h Another strategy is to pretend that the separation\h depends on behavior. As the flood began to occur,\h\h marine animals remained towards the bottom since\h they were already underwater, slow moving reptiles\h\h who couldn’t run to higher ground got caught in\h the middle, and of course fast humans are at the\h\h top because they ran up some hills. This might\h trick children, but it becomes ridiculous once\h\h you broaden the scope. Why are marine mammals\h way up towards the top? Weren’t they swimming\h\h with the ancient sharks? Why are flowering plants\h up towards the top as well? Can trees run? There\h\h is clearly no broad correlation of this kind. So apart from the complete impossibility of\h\h sediment deposition happening so quickly in the\h first place, the idea that fossils would happen to\h\h coincidentally sort into the precise layers that\h coincide with evolutionary predictions, with no\h\h exceptions, is beyond ridiculous. It is abundantly\h clear that fossils exist in layers that correspond\h\h to time periods in which they were alive. There is\h no other explanation. So the creationist reaction\h\h is often then to simply lie about what we have\h determined scientifically. They look for anomalous\h\h geological features and pretend that they disprove\h all of paleontology. This would include thrust\h\h faults where rock layers are pushed up due to\h tectonic activity, so as to appear to be younger\h\h than they really are. Creationists present this as\h specimens in younger layers than we would predict.\h\h But any geologist can easily match these strata\h with other occurrences of the same strata as\h\h they normally occur, and the fossils line up just\h fine. Also in some cases these uplifting events\h\h fold sections of strata upside down, seemingly\h reversing the order of the strata, but we also\h\h find things like animal burrows upside down in\h these strata, as though they dug up instead of\h\h down. These are clear indicators that the strata\h have been inverted by some geological process. And\h\h the fact remains that anomalous data, even when\h unexplained, which these features are not, still\h\h would not be enough to negate the overwhelming\h patterns we see in the fossil record. At a certain\h\h point creationists have to simply pretend that\h paleontologists and geologists are lying. This is\h\h as weak a defense as can be imagined, but it does\h work on some people, so it’s the way they have\h\h to go. Scientists are evil, so just ignore all\h scientific data. If not the scientists themselves,\h\h then the fossil record is a trick from Satan, or\h even a test of faith from god. The notion that\h\h such a gaslighting Ashton Kutcher-esque deity\h is all-loving or worthy of worship is rather\h\h comical. At the very least they just pretend that\h geological methods of dating are wrong, referring\h\h to an imagined tautology. The relative dating of\h strata is used to date fossils, and the fossils\h\h are used to date the layers, so it’s circular and\h unreliable. This is not the case, relative and\h\h absolute dating methods are completely different\h and they routinely corroborate each other. In the\h\h end, Young Earth creationists would have you\h believe that in 6000 years, over 99% of all\h\h life died, was rapidly deposited in sediments,\h and magically sorted itself into strata that\h\h couldn’t possibly have formed that fast and in a\h way that immaculately lines up with evolutionary\h\h principles even though evolution didn’t happen.\h It’s quite a leap of faith to say the least. In\h\h reality even a small child can understand that\h if we dig into lower strata, we go back in time,\h\h and we see things that are increasingly dissimilar\h to what we see today, along smooth morphological\h\h gradients that trace clear lineages over countless\h transitional forms for both plants and animals,\h\h that emerged and went extinct at certain\h times which match large-scale ecological\h\h events that are also well-substantiated. As bad as this all is for creationists,\h\h it gets even worse when you consider biogeography.\h This is the field that examines the geographical\h\h distribution of fossilized remains. As we already\h mentioned, certain forms are found exclusively in\h\h certain regions. This is obviously because they\h evolved in those regions. But creationists want\h\h us to believe that they walked from there all\h the way to the ark and then back, leaving no\h\h trace anywhere else. But we also now know due to\h plate tectonics that the continents were once all\h\h together. Combining predictions in geology with\h predictions in paleontology, if we know where\h\h the continents were once connected, and species\h that were around at that time, we should find\h\h the remains of those species in regions that are\h now nowhere near each other. This is a powerful\h\h prediction that was later confirmed, as we found\h remains of the same species in places like Western\h\h Africa and Eastern South America, as these once\h touched. This is what good science does, it brings\h\h together many different observations and explains\h them with a single model. That’s what evolution\h\h does to explain the sequence of fossilized remains\h as well as their locations, both stratigraphically\h\h and geographically. Everything fits precisely\h as expected, and in complete defiance of any\h\h expectation that creationists could have. For more elevated criticisms from intelligent\h\h design proponents, rather than lying about the\h existence of fossils or the geologic time they\h\h clearly outline, they will instead complain\h about portions of the fossil record that show\h\h morphological change which they claim is more\h rapid than evolutionary processes can explain,\h\h thus implying divine intervention. Of course\h the premiere example of this is the Cambrian\h\h explosion, which was a radiation event in\h which many new body plans first emerged.\h\h The dishonesty is more subtle here than with\h Young Earth creationists, but it is dishonesty\h\h nonetheless. We will\h\h see how this is not the case when we discuss\h molecular biology, such that there is plenty\h\h of time for evolutionary principles to operate. With the fossil record covered, let’s cover some\h\h more problems creationists face when trying to\h view the variety of life from a biblical lens.\h\h First, the people who wrote the bible were\h completely clueless when it comes to biology.\h\h Those who believe the bible was written by god\h are worshiping an allegedly omniscient god that\h\h had a practically non-existent understanding of\h his own creation. The populations on both sides of the ring\h\h are interfertile with their immediate neighboring\h populations, but where the two arms meet up again,\h\h those populations are unable to interbreed. Enough\h time has passed and enough change has occurred\h\h during these slow radiations that what was once\h a single species has become different species.\h Of course in response to this, a creationist\h would say that kind does not mean species,\h\h those are just different types of salamanders,\h so they are all in the salamander kind. But then there is no problem in terms\h\h of what is brought forth, as any new species will\h continue to belong to the same greater taxa, so it\h\h is an example of organisms bringing forth of their\h kind, and also an example of new species arising\h\h due to evolution. This “kind” could be the primate\h kind, or the mammal kind, or the vertebrate kind,\h\h or the eukaryote kind. No matter what branching\h event we identify on the tree of life, there is\h\h a taxon that encompasses everything that results\h from that point forward, and thus qualifies as\h\h a singular kind. Humans and chimpanzees are both\h of the ape kind. Humans and elephants are both of\h\h the mammal kind. Humans and sharks are both of the\h vertebrate kind. Humans and trees are both of the\h\h eukaryote kind. Everything is the same kind if you\h take kind to mean any taxonomic label imaginable,\h\h so everything does indeed bring forth\h of its kind, and also evolution is true.\h This is one of the key things that creationists\h need to understand. Evolution operates in\h\h terms of nested hierarchies. Wherever branching\h occurs, we identify specific clades, and all the\h\h descendants of a particular common ancestor are\h part of the clade, and will continue to be part\h\h of that clade forever in the future. That’s why\h humans are technically primates, and tetrapods,\h\h and even fish. All land animals evolved from bony\h fish, diverging around 400 million years ago. We\h\h do not refer to ourselves as fish, rather we use\h the name Osteichthyes. This is the clade that\h\h includes all bony fish and all tetrapods. We’re\h in there. If populations continue\h\h to diverge and significant speciation events\h occur, we need new taxa, so we simply create new\h\h labels. It’s like nested folders in your computer.\h Within one large folder, like the animal kingdom,\h\h you can have many smaller folders, like all the\h different phyla. Each of those can have folders\h\h as well, which might be subphyla, or classes.\h Things can get very complicated and messy,\h\h but the hierarchy is always there, and if the\h documents in a folder become too numerous and\h\h diverse, you will likely create some new folders\h to further organize your documents. The same goes\h\h for phylogeny, which in the end is an arbitrary\h system of classification invented by humans.\h Things get trickier when considering\h interbreeding. Wolf/dog hybrids,\h bison/cattle hybrids, various birds, it absolutely\h\h can happen. Populations diverge, sometimes\h retaining the ability to interbreed, sometimes\h\h losing that ability. Dogs and cats are different kinds,\h\h right? Well take a look at an extinct group\h of Carnivorans called miacids. That’s\h\h why some creationists resort to simply denying\h anything they are told about past organisms and\h\h the fossil record. Once again, it’s all lies from\h the devil. They want to see something happening\h\h today, with their own eyes. But there would\h be a limit to this, which may arrive some time in\h\h the future, where we end up having to distinguish\h radically different breeds as different species.\h\h They certainly can seem that way, or they would\h if you had never seen a dog before. They want to see a\h\h dog sprout wings, or fins, or additional limbs.\h First of all, this is not a reasonable request.\h\h All primates, for example, have the same body\h plan. Beyond\h\h this, organisms can indeed develop additional\h limbs or new types of limbs very quickly, but\h\h this will require molecular biology to explain,\h so we will get there in the next installment.\h To continue briefly on this thread, we should\h elucidate some related creationist terminology.\h\h Creationists will sometimes try to seem scholarly\h by acknowledging that some evolution does occur,\h\h but in limited fashion. Pivoting to another important demostration of\h\h evolution that creationists deny, we can discuss\h vestigial structures. It would\h be bizarre to think that a designer would give\h\h whales hip bones but no legs, yet it makes perfect\h sense in the context of evolution. It does some other minor thing, since\h nature is resourceful and makes the most of what\h\h it is working with. To summarize, designating\h something as vestigial does not mean it is\h\h functionless, even though every creationist will\h bring up minor functions for vestigial structures\h\h in an attempt to disprove its vestigial status.\h Now you can correct them. Their function has been completely lost. === FILE: The Definitive Guide to Debunking Creationists Part 4： Genetics⧸Molecular Biology [tfm9q4UoQBI].en.txt ===

So far in this series we have gone through the\h most common creationist talking points pertaining\h\h to cosmology, planetary science, abiogenesis,\h evolutionary biology, and paleontology. Let’s\h\h continue by zooming in to the molecular level,\h so that we can discuss evolution from the\h\h standpoint of genetics and molecular biology. Most creationists do not comprehend genetics\h\h on even a high school level. For this reason, it\h is very easy to run circles around less educated\h\h creationists within this unintuitive sphere. If\h they don’t understand what DNA is or what it does,\h\h it’s like shooting fish in a barrel. More\h sophisticated intelligent design proponents\h\h focus most of their propaganda on this area\h as well, because it is so much more esoteric,\h\h and lying with confidence about things\h that their targets don’t understand gives\h\h them a high probability of success. There’s\h lots to discuss here, so let’s get started.\h First we need to go over some background\h information. Creationists don’t understand\h\h genetics, but you should, so let’s hit the basics\h in ultra-abbreviated fashion. As always, I have\h\h tutorials on biochemistry and biology that explain\h everything we will discuss in greater detail,\h\h so head there after this series if you want to\h take the next step. For our purposes, let’s make\h\h sure we know what DNA is. DNA is a nucleic acid,\h which means it is a polymer of nucleotides. There\h\h are four different nucleotides in DNA, each made\h of a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base.\h\h These bases are abbreviated as A, T, C, and\h G. Nucleotides come together in different\h\h combinations to make DNA, which is made of two\h strands that coil together in a double helix,\h\h with the bases pointing towards each other in\h the interior. The way the two strands anneal is\h\h according to base pairing. A pairs with T and C\h with G. Every organism has a genome which is made\h\h of some number of chromosomes, which are very\h long DNA molecules with billions of base pairs,\h\h wrapped around proteins called histones.\h These chromosomes are the genetic code,\h\h which contains instructions for the assembly\h of the organism during embryonic development\h\h and its maintenance throughout its life. This occurs through transcription and translation.\h\h In transcription, small portions of the chromosome\h called genes are opened up by enzymes in order to\h\h generate an mRNA transcript. This occurs by the\h same rules of base pairing as for DNA, but mRNA\h\h is a little different. Then the mRNA is translated\h by a ribosome, again through simple base pairing,\h\h in order to generate a protein. This happens\h because the tRNA molecules that match up with\h\h the mRNA transcript, three bases at a time,\h are attached to specific amino acids, and the\h\h amino acids join together to form a polypeptide,\h which folds into a protein. Proteins do almost\h\h everything in your body. There are structural\h proteins, there are enzymes that do chemistry,\h\h there are receptor proteins that receive messages\h and trigger physiological functions, and so forth.\h One of the most important aspects of genetics\h for our purposes here is the way that the genome\h\h guides embryonic development to yield a particular\h type of animal. Unfortunately this is exceedingly\h\h complex, but we can at least describe Hox genes,\h which are a group of related genes that specify\h\h regions of the body plan along the head-tail axis\h of an animal. Encoded in these genes is the number\h\h and positions of limbs and other structures that\h will develop along the body. This is because the\h\h genes code for transcription factors, which are\h proteins that help turn other genes on and off by\h\h selectively binding to them, thus either promoting\h or inhibiting gene expression at hundreds of other\h\h sites on the genome. Because Hox genes have\h products that regulate so many other genes,\h\h changes to these genes can have dramatic\h effects on the developing organism’s body plan.\h With that covered, we now have to discuss\h mutations. Mutations describe changes to\h\h the genome. There are many different kinds of\h mutations and they can occur for many different\h\h reasons. The most simple mutations are point\h mutations. That is a change in just one base pair,\h\h from whichever base it was supposed to be to some\h other base. This can occur due to endogenous or\h\h exogenous mutagens. Carcinogens, UV light, or\h totally natural decay processes where radioactive\h\h nuclides within the body decay and produce a high\h energy particle that strikes a base in the genome\h\h of a particular cell. Errors can also occur\h during replication, where the enzyme creating\h\h the new strand makes a mistake. Repair enzymes\h exist to fix these errors, as well as the other\h\h mutations we described, but they don’t catch\h them all, so point mutations happen in every\h\h organism all the time. Most are neutral, many of\h the rest are harmful, and some are beneficial. It\h\h depends on whether any of the amino acids in the\h resulting protein change, and how that affects the\h\h function of that protein. If it’s an enzyme,\h it could function more efficiently. Or less.\h\h Or it could lose function. Or even change\h functions if several mutations accumulate.\h We have to understand some other types\h of mutations that can occur. There are\h\h mutations like insertions and deletions that\h change the reading frame of the gene, which\h\h usually result in a non-functional protein. But\h there are also macromutations. Very significant\h\h changes to the genome can sometimes occur. For\h example, gene duplication. During replication,\h\h the enzyme can copy a section of DNA more than\h once. Additionally, during crossing over between\h\h homologous chromosomes in meiosis, a type\h of cell division, misalignment can result\h\h in two copies of the same gene getting into one\h chromosome. With two copies of the same gene,\h\h neofunctionalization is now possible. One copy of\h the gene can be retained, while the other gene can\h\h slowly accumulate mutations and therefore\h yield a totally different protein product.\h\h No function is lost, while a new one can be\h gained, and studies show that around 50% of\h\h gene duplications lead to functional divergence. A similar situation occurs with orphan genes,\h\h or de novo genes. There are sections of DNA\h called promoters which sit next to the coding\h\h region of a gene that an enzyme will interact\h with, resulting in transcription of the gene.\h\h A mutation event can sometimes rearrange sections\h of the chromosome which result in a promoter being\h\h placed next to a previously non-coding section of\h DNA. This results in a brand new gene instantly,\h\h with a totally random sequence and therefore\h a totally random protein product. This protein\h\h might be useless, but it might not, and any modest\h functionality can be subsequently molded through\h\h natural selection. The potentiality of a process\h like gene duplication is magnified tremendously\h\h when entire chromosomes duplicate. This is again\h typically due to errors during cell division,\h\h where homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids\h don’t separate during meiosis so one cell ends up\h\h with multiple copies of the same chromosome. This\h leads to the possibility of many different genes\h\h going through neofunctionalization, which\h can have dramatic effects for an organism.\h Now if any of these mutations occur in the somatic\h cells of an organism, the effect is usually minor.\h\h But if they occur in the germline cells of the\h organism, or the cells that produce gametes,\h\h meaning sperm and eggs, then we are looking at\h the offspring having a significantly different\h\h genotype than the parents, and thus potentially\h a different phenotype, which refers to actual\h\h morphological differences. These are typically\h very tiny, but sometimes not so tiny. It simply\h\h depends on how those proteins influence embryonic\h development and the determination of the body\h\h plan. We have physically observed instances where\h even single point mutations can have drastic\h\h effects on an animal’s morphology, like legs\h growing from a fly’s head instead of antennae,\h\h extra pairs of wings, and other major changes.\h The implications for evolution are obvious.\h With this understood we can now begin to outline\h the various mechanisms by which evolution\h\h operates. Whereas Darwin envisioned only natural\h selection, over the 150 years since, we now\h\h know that there are many other mechanisms also at\h play. Apart from mutation, which produces genetic\h\h variety, and natural selection, where organisms\h better suited for survival and reproduction have\h\h their genes more likely to proliferate, there\h are a few other important ones. Genetic drift\h\h describes a change in the relative frequency of\h an allele in a population due to chance and random\h\h sampling. An allele is a copy of a gene. Most\h animals have two copies of every gene, one from\h\h each parent, and each copy is called an allele.\h Alleles can be dominant or recessive, and this\h\h genotype can dictate the phenotype, or the version\h of a particular trait that is expressed on the\h\h organism. There is also gene flow, which describes\h the movement of genes from one population to\h\h another, often due to migration, which can\h increase genetic diversity. Then there is sexual\h\h selection, or non-random mating based on perceived\h evolutionary fitness. This operates by criteria\h\h that are quite different from survivability, and\h can produce interesting morphological features.\h\h Horizontal gene transfer, niche construction,\h epigenetics, the list is long and we need not\h\h dwell on every detail for our purposes. As we can see, evolution relies largely on\h\h population dynamics, and changes that occur on\h the genetic level which Darwin could never have\h\h understood in his time, before we even knew\h that DNA existed. Creationists relentlessly\h\h talk about Darwinism and Darwinian evolution and\h in general never shut up about Darwin for this\h\h specific reason. He lived a long time ago before\h we actually understood evolution, so they will\h\h try to present evolution in this primitive lens.\h Young Earth creationists and intelligent design\h\h advocates alike will always return to the same\h mantra, random mutation and natural selection\h\h are insufficient in producing the variety of\h life. They will all say this every chance they\h\h get. And yet, even with the couple of minutes\h of background information we just went over,\h\h we can immediately see how dishonest this is.\h When they say random mutation, they mean point\h\h mutations. These are more limited in scope. They\h are ignoring macromutations like gene duplication,\h\h de novo genes, or chromosome duplication,\h which produce significant discrepancies\h\h in the genome in a single generation.\h And when they say natural selection,\h\h they are limiting evolution to a singular\h mechanism, ignoring the others we described.\h\h This is a deliberate misrepresentation of the\h scope and potentiality of evolutionary processes.\h More detailed attempts to misrepresent genetics\h will take advantage of the negative connotation of\h\h the word “mutation” to pretend that all mutations\h are harmful. They will say things like “mutations\h\h degrade genetic information”, as though a bucket\h of toxic green goo has fallen on the DNA and is\h\h giving it chemical burns. In reality mutations are\h simply changes to the genetic code. As we said,\h\h with point mutations, the vast majority are\h neutral. The mutation does not result in any\h\h change whatsoever to the protein product. Of the\h remaining possibilities, some are harmful and some\h\h are beneficial, we have to look at the change made\h to the protein. Is the amino acid that changed in\h\h the active site of an enzyme? Does this cause it\h to bind to its substrate more tightly? Or not at\h\h all? Any of these possibilities could be bad or\h good, depending on the situation. Significantly\h\h harmful mutations are not often observed because\h those organisms tend to die quickly without\h\h reproducing, so we disproportionately observe\h beneficial mutations and improved function, which\h\h can appear like design to the unprepared mind. Another creationist fixation has to do with\h\h probability. They will take any enzyme, like say\h DNA polymerase, and remark how unlikely it is for\h\h that to have arisen by chance. In order to make it\h seem impossible, they will play a devious numbers\h\h game. They’ll say: Here’s an enzyme with 300 amino\h acid residues, there are 20 amino acids, so the\h\h probability of this precise sequence evolving\h by chance is one in 20 to the 300th power. Their\h\h targets will gasp at the infinitesimal odds, and\h conclude that it can only exist because god willed\h\h it so. This is ridiculous. That precise sequence\h is far from the only sequence that will perform\h\h that function. Many of the amino acids in the\h active site of an enzyme have limited variability,\h\h although even those have some, but the rest of\h the amino acids contribute only to the overall\h\h shape of the enzyme, and thus have tremendous\h variability. There are sets of amino acids that\h\h are extremely similar. Amino acids have the\h same general structure plus a variable side\h\h chain. Here are a few that have an alkyl side\h chain, meaning they consist of only carbon and\h\h hydrogen. Anywhere we find one of these, we could\h easily swap to another similar one and the effect\h\h on the enzyme would be practically non-existent.\h Only if we switched from something like a\h\h hydrophobic to a hydrophilic side chain, like\h alkyl to one containing a hydroxyl group,\h\h could that potentially have an impact on\h the folding pattern, and even then it is\h\h unlikely to be significant. So we are saying\h that the majority of the amino acid residues\h\h could be completely different, and the function\h would be identical or similar. Furthermore,\h\h new enzymes don’t have to function optimally. They\h can perform a function with moderate efficiency\h\h and then get refined by natural selection\h over time. And finally, we know for a fact\h\h that many different sequences can perform the\h same function, because different organisms have\h\h different versions of the same enzymes. Looking\h again at DNA polymerase, different organisms have\h\h different polymerase enzymes. They have different\h sequences, and we give them different names,\h\h yet they all copy DNA. With genetic engineering\h we manipulate the amino acid sequence of enzymes\h\h to make them perform more efficiently than\h the natural counterpart. There is tremendous\h\h variability and nothing is perfect in the first\h place. So this is lazy propaganda on the part of\h\h creationists. Nature creates many sequences,\h stumbles upon functional sequences by chance,\h\h and those are optimized and amplified by natural\h selection. Plenty of research has been done\h\h which corroborates the fact that totally random\h sequences are an abundant source of bioactive RNA\h\h and peptides. This is not controversial. Recalling the creationist claim that\h\h microevolution is possible but not macroevolution,\h this seems even more ridiculous in the light of\h\h molecular biology. There is no mechanistic\h distinction between the two, it’s all based\h\h on mutations. We already explained how certain\h point mutations and especially macromutations\h\h can produce significant morphological change even\h in a single generation. Continuing with embryonic development, a favorite\h\h creationist talking point is to reference the\h early history of embryology. In the 19th century,\h\h Ernst Haeckel pioneered this field by observing\h the embryos of many different species and\h\h hand-drawing their development at various stages.\h Comparing these developmental pathways offers many\h\h clues regarding evolutionary relationships,\h since many aspects of development are shared\h\h between distantly related animals. For example,\h all chordates, including mammals, birds, reptiles,\h\h amphibians, fish, tunicates, and lancelets, have\h a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal\h\h arches, a post-anal tail, and an endostyle or\h thyroid gland at some point in their development.\h\h Some chordates have all of these characteristics\h as adults, like lancelets, but others lose at\h\h least some of them later on. For example, humans\h lack an intact notochord, pharyngeal arches,\h\h and post-anal tail. By this we mean that a mammal doesn’t\h\h go through a specific fish stage, followed by\h an amphibian stage, and then a reptile stage,\h\h and so forth. They\h look more or less just like Haeckel’s drawings.\h Moving on, there are some classic arguments\h from intelligent design proponents that must\h\h be neutralized. The first is the so-called waiting\h time problem. This one says that adaptations which\h\h require multiple mutations are impossible because\h of the improbability of those specific mutations\h\h occurring in a reasonable time span. Mutations occur\h and they are either selected for or they aren’t.\h\h And these mutations do not have to occur in\h a specific sequence, they could occur in any\h\h sequence across an entire population and then come\h together during the recombination phase of sexual\h\h reproduction, such that each parent can have one\h mutation and the offspring has both. Furthermore,\h\h the idea that each individual mutation can’t be\h selected for because only the entire set confers\h\h the beneficial adaptation is incorrect. Individual\h mutations could still confer a slight survival\h\h advantage and therefore proliferate statistically. A similar argument from ID proponents is that of\h\h irreducible complexity. This states that some\h biological structures are so complex, with so\h\h many interconnected parts, that it can’t possibly\h have evolved, because removing just one component\h\h renders the structure unusable, and therefore\h none of the individual components can have been\h\h selected for, such that it could have arisen\h piecemeal. A sudden dramatic change, like\h deleting an entire population of organisms,\h\h has a much bigger impact. The same goes for any cellular component. In general, the pseudoscientific nature of\h\h intelligent design can be exposed simply by asking\h its proponents to put forward a rigorous model.\h\h Which biological structures are designed? Intelligent design is just a god of\h the gaps argument in a tuxedo, nothing more.\h Another aspect of genetics that creationists lie\h about is the proportion of the genome that is\h\h functional. In reality,\h\h it is possible for soft tissue to be preserved\h under the right conditions. The process by which\h\h soft tissue decays depends on contact with\h air and water. But this soft tissue was in\h\h the dry interior of the specimen, stabilized by\h contact with hemoglobin and the mineral walls\h\h of the surrounding pores. Though fascinating,\h it does not change the dating of the specimen.\h In general, out of everything we could summarize\h regarding genetics and molecular biology, and how\h\h these fields corroborate evolutionary principles\h far beyond reasonable doubt, we certainly can\h\h focus on mutations, embryonic development, and\h other such complex topics. But we also can simply\h\h point to heredity. This is something most people\h can wrap their heads around. Your genome is very\h\h similar to those of your parents, because it is\h a combination of the genomes of your parents.\h\h That’s how paternity tests work, on the basis of\h genetic similarity. Using the principle of genetic\h\h similarity, we can tell who your father is, and\h your father’s father, and his father before him,\h\h and so forth. When an organism develops an\h entirely new gene, that gene will continue to\h\h show up in its entire pool of descendants if the\h organism is reproductively successful. There are countless\h\h ways to confirm evolutionary lineages that make\h no sense whatsoever in the context of design.\h We can expand this way of thinking to any genome\h as a whole. The more related two\h species are on the tree of life, the greater the\h\h genetic similarity and the more enzymes they have\h in common. These are facts that do not “disprove”\h\h design, but when absolutely every aspect of\h biology conforms flawlessly to evolutionary\h\h principles, what room is left then, for this\h god of the gaps that creationists would have\h\h you believe in? Not much room at all, in fact. And with that we conclude the rigorously\h\h scientific portion of this series. At this point in the series, we’ve covered an\h enormous range of fallacious talking points that\h\h creationists employ, from cosmology all the way\h to molecular biology. Let’s finish things up by\h\h reviewing arguments that creationists put forward\h which are not necessarily based in discrediting\h\h scientific data, but are rather more philosophical\h or theological in nature. It turns out that\h\h creationists are not just allergic to science, but\h also to basic logic, and this shines through in\h\h its purest form when the arguments are intended\h to be of a more basal nature than scientific\h\h inquiry. Let’s start out with the existence of\h\h the universe, which we alluded to in part\h one but left for later. All creationists,\h\h top to bottom, insist that the existence of the\h universe is totally nonsensical without a deity\h\h to have created it. If they are comfortable with their deity\h simply existing, why can’t the universe simply\h\h exist? There is no consistency to their logic. The more intellectual creationist will attempt\h\h to identify some logical loophole to justify\h this privileged status for their deity. The\h\h universe began to exist, so it needs a cause, but\h their deity did not begin to exist. He simply has\h\h always existed, or exists outside of time, so\h no cause is required. These justifications,\h\h existing infinitely into the past, or existence\h without time, are precisely as absurd as a\h\h universe existing without cause. There is no basis\h for presuming that such things are possible. And\h\h even if we were to entertain the notion of a deity\h existing, it would not be their specific deity,\h\h which can be disproved in countless other\h ways that go beyond the scope of this series.\h We can all admit that existence is a mystery. In the realm of pure philosophy, great thinkers\h\h like Leibniz, Wittgenstein, Hume, and Heidegger\h have pondered the problem of existence. It is\h\h puzzling that anything exists rather than nothing.\h Hume in particular argued that although our\h\h experience is dominated by causality, perhaps the\h formation of the universe is fundamentally outside\h\h of our experience and may be exempt from this\h guideline. Pivoting to philosophy of science,\h\h or at least misuse of scientific terminology,\h many creationists will abuse the word “theory”.\h\h Preachers in particular will exclaim\h that evolution is a theory, not a law,\h\h or a fact. Therefore, it’s never been proven.\h This is preposterous. Gravity, for example,\h\h factually exists. Gravity is a natural phenomenon,\h\h which factually exists, and can be described by\h laws or theories. Furthermore, theories are more\h\h powerful than laws. Newton’s equation is simply a\h summary of observations. It has predictive power,\h\h but no explanatory power. Relativity has both.\h It predicts everything Newton’s equation does\h\h and much more, but also explains what gravity\h is, the influence of the curvature of spacetime.\h\h In science, theories are better than laws. We can\h say the same about evolution. Evolution factually\h\h happens. We observe evolution every single day. We\h observe how genetic information changes over time,\h\h how the distribution of alleles changes\h over time, we observe speciation events. We\h\h observe evolution. Evolution happens. There is no\h arguing this. What creationists mean, of course,\h\h is that it isn’t proven that all life evolved\h from a common ancestor over several billion\h\h years. That’s where evolutionary theory comes\h in. Just as gravity is a natural phenomenon\h\h that can be described by a theory, evolution is\h also a natural phenomenon that can be described\h\h by a theory. Evolutionary theory explains how\h evolution occurs. It used to be limited to natural\h\h selection in Darwin’s time. This was broadened and\h labeled neo-Darwinism in the early 20th century,\h\h and by the end of the 20th century it came to be\h known as the modern synthesis. That is our current\h\h theory of evolution, one which is still growing\h today as new mechanisms are discovered. It is not\h\h a guess. Theories are not guesses or opinions.\h Theories are models that correlate large amounts\h\h of disparate data, elegantly explain all of this\h data at once, and make concrete, quantifiable,\h\h falsifiable predictions. That’s what our\h evolutionary model does. It takes the diversity\h\h of life, the fossil record, genetics, and so many\h other aspects of biology, and explains them with a\h\h single model. This model makes predictions, like\h the genetic similarity we should expect based\h\h on phylogenetic relatedness, or the locations of\h certain fossils based on biogeography, and so much\h\h more. Evolution as a theory, which explains the\h diversity of life, is consistent beyond reasonable\h\h doubt just like the theory of relativity.\h Creationism does not do any of this. Creationism\h\h is blind faith, coupled with a willful ignorance\h of scientific principles which contradict that\h\h blind faith. === FILE: The Development of Plate Tectonics [oTrnz4Yy5m8].en.txt ===

Now that we understand the composition of the Earth, it’s time to get a closer look at some important geological processes, starting with plate tectonics. Plate tectonics may sound like a fancy food in a gastropub, but it’s actually a thoroughly corroborated theory describing how Earth’s outermost layer, the lithosphere, slides around on top of the ductile portion of the upper mantle, the asthenosphere. Plate tectonics is responsible for everything from the striking peaks of the Himalayas to the underwater smokers along mid-ocean ridges. So how did this theory come to be? The story begins with an astronomer named Alfred Wegener. Dr. Wegener earned his PhD in astronomy at the University of Berlin in 1904. In an odd turn of events, he spent most of his career studying the weather of very cold places, like Greenland. In 1911, Dr. Wegener came across a paper on the presence of similar Permian-aged fossils in disparate places like South America and Africa, or Antarctica and Australia. He concluded that the only way these organisms could have existed together would be if all the continents had been joined together into one huge supercontinent, which he named Pangea. Unfortunately, Dr. Wegener died of overexertion during one of his Greenland expeditions before he could substantiate Pangea’s existence. In fact, the idea of Pangea and the theory of plate tectonics that it relied upon was resoundingly rejected throughout much of the 20th century. Further evidence for plate tectonics came in the 1950s during the study of magnetic minerals in rocks. When an igneous rock crystallizes, tiny needles of the mineral magnetite align themselves parallel to Earth’s magnetic field lines, and studying the orientation of these “magnetic fossils”, so to speak, makes it possible to reconstruct Earth’s magnetic field over time. Now, Earth’s magnetic field does somewhat drift around the poles, but the study of these magnetic rocks seemed to indicate that over the past 500 million years, Earth’s south magnetic pole drifted from the northern hemisphere, through the equator, and to its present location over the geographic south pole. But the magnetic poles must be located near the geographic poles because the magnetic field is strongly related to Earth’s rotation. Therefore, this observation could only be explained by the movement of the continents themselves over a semi-stationary field. Throughout World War II, geologists used sonar to map the ocean floor and were shocked by the topography they discovered. The ocean floor wasn’t a flat plain, but rather was full of mountain ridges with perpendicular fractures, deep trenches, and long chains of underwater volcanoes. Based on this data, Harold Hess, a geologist from Princeton University and former World War II submarine sonar operator, proposed a theory for how continents might move. Hess postulated that the linear volcanic ridges at the centers of oceans were caused by areas of convection-driven, hot, rising mantle that solidified and spread out laterally to create new oceanic crust. Evidence for this included low seismic velocities, the presence of volcanoes, and high heat flow from the mantle at these mid-ocean ridges. Once formed, oceanic crust moves away from the ridge, cooling and becoming more dense with age until it eventually sinks back into the mantle at deep sea trenches. According to Hess’s theory, the simultaneous creation of oceanic crust at mid ocean ridges, and its destruction at subduction zones, would limit the age of the world’s ocean basins to a few hundred million years, which agreed with the relatively thin layer of pelagic sediment on the seafloor. Though the evidence described so far may seem convincing, it was still only circumstantial at the time, but not for long. The smoking gun would eventually come from the discovery of magnetic striping of the seafloor. Prior to this discovery, paleomagnetism had been extensively studied in terrestrial rocks and it was well known that the Earth’s magnetic field periodically reversed. The current configuration of the magnetic field is said to be “normal” polarity and the flipped polarity is called “reverse”. Paradoxically, the magnetic pole located at the north pole today is actually the magnetic south pole, since magnetic field lines always point from the north to the south pole of a magnet. At any rate, if Hess was right, the magnetic striping along the seafloor would be mirrored across the ridge and correspond to the already known record of magnetic reversals, and in 1963, Fred Vine and his PhD advisor Drummond Matthews provided the evidence, leading to the wide acceptance of the theory of plate tectonics. While Dr. Hess’s work explained the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches, there were still two pesky questions left unexplained. First, how were seamounts formed, like the Hawaiian Islands, and second, what created long perpendicular fractures along mid ocean ridges, as exemplified along the South Atlantic Ridge? In 1963 Canadian geologist J. Tuzo Wilson figured out the answer. He proposed that seamounts were formed due to volcanism induced by a cylindrical, stationary area of hot, rising mantle called hotspots, or more specifically, mantle plumes. Using the Hawaiian Islands and the Emperor seamounts as an example, Dr. Wilson observed that the alignment of the island chains followed the motion of the Pacific plate, which led him to develop the following understanding of seamounts. At some point in time, a mantle plume forms beneath an area of the crust which leads to the initiation of volcanism. Then over millions of years, the plate moves steadily over the stationary mantle plume, leaving a long trail of inactive volcanic islands behind a front of active volcanism, which is where the islands are created. As an area of the crust moves off the hotspot, volcanism shuts off and the seamount begins to be slowly eroded by the sea. When looking at a satellite image of the Pacific Ocean, you can see a chain of increasingly eroded seamounts extending all the way from Hawaii, which is currently beneath the plume, to the Aleutians. This is a precise recording of the Pacific plate’s motion over the past 65 million years, called a hotspot track. Interestingly, it is not linear, but is shaped like a hockey stick, which beautifully illustrates a sudden change in plate motion that occurred around 40 million years ago. Two years after proposing mantle plumes, Dr. Wilson suggested an explanation for the perpendicular faults along mid ocean ridges. Mid-ocean ridges don’t form in a single continuous line, but are made up of hundreds of ridge segments. Each ridge segment is connected to its neighbor by a perpendicular feature called a transform fault, which is just a type of strike-slip fault that connects two plate boundaries. When new crust is formed along a mid-ocean ridge, transform faults form to accommodate changes in the spreading rate along the ridge. With these two final questions answered, Dr. Wilson proposed a unified theory of plate tectonics, combing Hess’s ideas with his own. Today, the theory of plate tectonics is accepted by any serious geologist and has been expanded upon to explain the periodic creation and destruction of single-continent land masses called supercontinents. That cycle, the Wilson cycle, is what we will tackle next, so let’s move forward and learn more about tectonic plates.

=== FILE: The Difference Between Fiscal and Monetary Policy [o0Yt6buayZ4].en.txt ===

More often than not, both economists\h and politicians are constantly worried\h\h about high unemployment and high inflation.\h Whenever a government tries to prevent these\h\h it has two ways of doing so: fiscal policy\h and monetary policy. Any time the government\h tries to increase output in an economy, or speed\h\h up economic growth, that’s known as expansionary\h policy. Monetary\h\h policy is the way central banks influence the\h economy through the management of the money supply\h\h and interest rates. First of all, governments can\h influence how money is created. It’s important to\h\h understand that money creation does not mean\h the government prints new coins and paper\h\h bills.
